Washington: Office of the Federal Register has issued the following notice:

AGENCY:
Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, Department of Commerce.

SUMMARY:
On October 19, 2026, the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) Secretariat issued a Notice of Final Panel Action. The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) is notifying the public that the NAFTA Binational Panel's final judgment is not in harmony with Commerce's final determination in the countervailing duty (CVD) investigation of certain softwood lumber products (lumber) from Canada, and that Commerce is amending the final determination and the resulting CVD order with respect to the countervailable subsidy rate assigned to Canfor Corporation (Canfor); J.D. Irving, Limited (J.D. Irving); Resolute FP Canada Inc. (Resolute); Tolko Marketing and Sales Ltd. (Tolko); West Fraser Mills Ltd. (West Fraser); and all other companies.

DATES:
Applicable October 29, 2026.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Samuel Brummitt, AD/CVD Operations, Office III, Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, U.S. Department of Commerce, 1401 Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20230; telephone: (202) 482-7851.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Background
On November 8, 2017, Commerce published its Final Determination in the CVD investigation of lumber from Canada.[1] The Final Determination was subsequently amended.[2] Respondent parties subsequently challenged Commerce's final determination before the NAFTA Binational Panel, pursuant to Article 1904 of NAFTA. The parties briefed and argued the case before the Panel and, on March 6, 2024, the Panel issued its decision, affirming in part and remanding in part Commerce's determination.[3] On December 17, 2024, Commerce issued its First Remand Determination.[4] On March 6, 2026, the Panel issued its decision on remand, affirming in part and remanding in part Commerce's First Remand Determination.[5] On June 17, 2026, Commerce issued its Second Remand Determination.[6] By decision on October 5, 2026, the NAFTA Panel affirmed Commerce's Second Remand Determination.[7] On October 19, 2026, the Panel directed the NAFTA Secretariat to issue a Notice of Final Panel Action; the NAFTA Secretariat subsequently issued the Notice of Final Panel Action on October 19, 2026.

Timken Notice
In its decision in Timken,[8] as clarified by Diamond Sawblades,[9] the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit held that, pursuant to sections 516A(c) and (e) of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended (the Act), Commerce must publish a notice of court decision that is not “in harmony” with a Commerce determination and must suspend liquidation of entries pending a “conclusive” court decision. Because NAFTA panels step into the shoes of the courts they are replacing, they must apply the law of the national court that would otherwise review the administrative determination. Therefore, we are publishing notice that the NAFTA Panel's Panel Decision on Second Remand, as memorialized by the NAFTA Secretariat's October 19, 2026, Notice of Final Panel Action, is “not in harmony” with the Final Determination.[10] Publication of this notice fulfills the obligation imposed upon Commerce by the decision in Timken.

Amended Final Determination
Having received a Notice of Final Panel Action from the NAFTA Secretariat, Commerce is amending its Final Determination with respect to Canfor, J.D. Irving, Resolute, Tolko, West Fraser, and all other producers and exporters as follows:

Company Original final determination subsidy rate (percent) Subsidy rate post- notice of final action (percent)
Canfor Corporation and its cross-owned affiliates11 13.24 12.49
J.D. Irving Limited and its cross-owned affiliates12 3.34 2.96
Resolute FP Canada Inc. and its cross-owned affiliates13 14.70 13.90
Tolko Marketing and Sales Ltd. and its cross-owned affiliates14 14.85 11.01
West Fraser Mills Ltd. and its cross-owned affiliates15 17.99 16.73
All Others 14.19 12.80
( printed page 69243)
Cash Deposit Requirements
Commerce will issue revised cash deposit instructions to U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP). Because Canfor J.D. Irving, Resolute, Tolko, and West Fraser have superseding cash deposit rates, i.e., there have been final results published in a subsequent administrative review, this notice will not affect the current cash deposit rate for Canfor J.D. Irving, Resolute, Tolko, and West Fraser. For all other companies that do not have a superseding cash deposit rate, Commerce will issue revised cash deposit instructions to CBP.

Notification to Interested Parties
This notice is issued and published in accordance with sections 516A(c) and (e) and 777(i)(1) of the Act.

Dated: October 28, 2026.

Scot Fullerton,

Acting Deputy Assistant Secretary for Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Operations.

Washington: Office of the Federal Register has issued the following notice:

AGENCY:
Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, Department of Commerce.

SUMMARY:
On October 19, 2026, the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) Secretariat issued a Notice of Final Panel Action. The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) is notifying the public that the NAFTA Binational Panel's final judgment is not in harmony with Commerce's final determination in the countervailing duty (CVD) investigation of certain softwood lumber products (lumber) from Canada, and that Commerce is amending the final determination and the resulting CVD order with respect to the countervailable subsidy rate assigned to Canfor Corporation (Canfor); J.D. Irving, Limited (J.D. Irving); Resolute FP Canada Inc. (Resolute); Tolko Marketing and Sales Ltd. (Tolko); West Fraser Mills Ltd. (West Fraser); and all other companies.

DATES:
Applicable October 29, 2026.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Samuel Brummitt, AD/CVD Operations, Office III, Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, U.S. Department of Commerce, 1401 Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20230; telephone: (202) 482-7851.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Background
On November 8, 2017, Commerce published its Final Determination in the CVD investigation of lumber from Canada.[1] The Final Determination was subsequently amended.[2] Respondent parties subsequently challenged Commerce's final determination before the NAFTA Binational Panel, pursuant to Article 1904 of NAFTA. The parties briefed and argued the case before the Panel and, on March 6, 2024, the Panel issued its decision, affirming in part and remanding in part Commerce's determination.[3] On December 17, 2024, Commerce issued its First Remand Determination.[4] On March 6, 2026, the Panel issued its decision on remand, affirming in part and remanding in part Commerce's First Remand Determination.[5] On June 17, 2026, Commerce issued its Second Remand Determination.[6] By decision on October 5, 2026, the NAFTA Panel affirmed Commerce's Second Remand Determination.[7] On October 19, 2026, the Panel directed the NAFTA Secretariat to issue a Notice of Final Panel Action; the NAFTA Secretariat subsequently issued the Notice of Final Panel Action on October 19, 2026.

Timken Notice
In its decision in Timken,[8] as clarified by Diamond Sawblades,[9] the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit held that, pursuant to sections 516A(c) and (e) of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended (the Act), Commerce must publish a notice of court decision that is not “in harmony” with a Commerce determination and must suspend liquidation of entries pending a “conclusive” court decision. Because NAFTA panels step into the shoes of the courts they are replacing, they must apply the law of the national court that would otherwise review the administrative determination. Therefore, we are publishing notice that the NAFTA Panel's Panel Decision on Second Remand, as memorialized by the NAFTA Secretariat's October 19, 2026, Notice of Final Panel Action, is “not in harmony” with the Final Determination.[10] Publication of this notice fulfills the obligation imposed upon Commerce by the decision in Timken.

Amended Final Determination
Having received a Notice of Final Panel Action from the NAFTA Secretariat, Commerce is amending its Final Determination with respect to Canfor, J.D. Irving, Resolute, Tolko, West Fraser, and all other producers and exporters as follows:

Company Original final determination subsidy rate (percent) Subsidy rate post- notice of final action (percent)
Canfor Corporation and its cross-owned affiliates11 13.24 12.49
J.D. Irving Limited and its cross-owned affiliates12 3.34 2.96
Resolute FP Canada Inc. and its cross-owned affiliates13 14.70 13.90
Tolko Marketing and Sales Ltd. and its cross-owned affiliates14 14.85 11.01
West Fraser Mills Ltd. and its cross-owned affiliates15 17.99 16.73
All Others 14.19 12.80
( printed page 69243)
Cash Deposit Requirements
Commerce will issue revised cash deposit instructions to U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP). Because Canfor J.D. Irving, Resolute, Tolko, and West Fraser have superseding cash deposit rates, i.e., there have been final results published in a subsequent administrative review, this notice will not affect the current cash deposit rate for Canfor J.D. Irving, Resolute, Tolko, and West Fraser. For all other companies that do not have a superseding cash deposit rate, Commerce will issue revised cash deposit instructions to CBP.

Notification to Interested Parties
This notice is issued and published in accordance with sections 516A(c) and (e) and 777(i)(1) of the Act.

Dated: October 28, 2026.

Scot Fullerton,

Acting Deputy Assistant Secretary for Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Operations.

María Chivite, Socialist President of Navarra , was in Argentina a few months before the general elections of 2023 to meet with Lorena Suárez , the former leader of the PSOE in the South American country from 2022 to 2024, during which she promoted the Grandchildren's Law that facilitated the naturalization of foreigners by providing crucial information and advice.

In a video consulted by Libertad Digital from November 20, 2022, with the 2023 general elections in mind, the President of Navarra celebrated the naturalizations facilitated by the Grandchildren's Law and the elimination of the "rogued vote" . Chivite noted that the purpose of her visit was to connect with the Navarrese community in Argentina, sending them "a very big greeting and lots of affection." "The truth is that it has been a very emotional visit, and I didn't want to miss the opportunity to visit here at the headquarters to be with my fellow PSOE members in Argentina . I send you all a very affectionate greeting."

The Navarrese president celebrated the nationalizations under the Grandchildren's Law and the elimination of the rogued vote from Argentina, stating: "I encourage you to continue working on these new windows of opportunity and recognition of rights like the Democratic Memory Law and the disappearance of the rogued voting system, recognizing the rights of Navarrese also in Argentina. A big kiss."

This is not the first electoral tour for the Navarrese president. María Chivite traveled this October to Peru and Argentina just a month before the elections to recruit voters that the socialists lack in Spain. In fact, the PSOE won the last seat for Navarra in the general elections on July 23, 2023, by a margin of 2,855 votes against Sumar, in an election where Pedro Sánchez maintained power by the narrowest of margins. This information is not lost on Chivite, who is visiting strategic countries where a handful more votes can be crucial in the elections.

PSOE Maneuvers in South America

In this regard, it is important to remember that the PSOE and the government of Pedro Sánchez have been very active in electoral matters in Argentina. They have not only offered free advice to newly naturalized citizens but even regional leaders such as José Ramón Gómez Besteiro (Galicia) and Adrián Barbón (Asturias) have traveled to the South American country in recent months to mobilize the electorate residing abroad. Similarly, the Minister of Education, Milagros Tolón, visited the Galician and Spanish community residing in Buenos Aires just days after Pedro Sánchez called elections for November 29.

In these elections, the overseas vote may be decisive, as Violeta Alonso, Pedro Sánchez's liaison for the Grandchildren's Law abroad, acknowledged this week by urging people to vote , stating that if Spanish citizens residing abroad and those naturalized under the Grandchildren's Law mobilize, it will have a "significant impact" on the elections.
lseg:urn:newsml:newsroom:20261104:nNRA2k.texto:
María Chivite, Socialist President of Navarra , was in Argentina a few months before the general elections of 2023 to meet with Lorena Suárez , the former leader of the PSOE in the South American country from 2022 to 2024, during which she promoted the Grandchildren's Law that facilitated the naturalization of foreigners by providing crucial information and advice.

In a video consulted by Libertad Digital from November 20, 2022, with the 2023 general elections in mind, the President of Navarra celebrated the naturalizations facilitated by the Grandchildren's Law and the elimination of the "rogued vote" . Chivite noted that the purpose of her visit was to connect with the Navarrese community in Argentina, sending them "a very big greeting and lots of affection." "The truth is that it has been a very emotional visit, and I didn't want to miss the opportunity to visit here at the headquarters to be with my fellow PSOE members in Argentina . I send you all a very affectionate greeting."

The Navarrese president celebrated the nationalizations under the Grandchildren's Law and the elimination of the rogued vote from Argentina, stating: "I encourage you to continue working on these new windows of opportunity and recognition of rights like the Democratic Memory Law and the disappearance of the rogued voting system, recognizing the rights of Navarrese also in Argentina. A big kiss."

This is not the first electoral tour for the Navarrese president. María Chivite traveled this October to Peru and Argentina just a month before the elections to recruit voters that the socialists lack in Spain. In fact, the PSOE won the last seat for Navarra in the general elections on July 23, 2023, by a margin of 2,855 votes against Sumar, in an election where Pedro Sánchez maintained power by the narrowest of margins. This information is not lost on Chivite, who is visiting strategic countries where a handful more votes can be crucial in the elections.

PSOE Maneuvers in South America

In this regard, it is important to remember that the PSOE and the government of Pedro Sánchez have been very active in electoral matters in Argentina. They have not only offered free advice to newly naturalized citizens but even regional leaders such as José Ramón Gómez Besteiro (Galicia) and Adrián Barbón (Asturias) have traveled to the South American country in recent months to mobilize the electorate residing abroad. Similarly, the Minister of Education, Milagros Tolón, visited the Galician and Spanish community residing in Buenos Aires just days after Pedro Sánchez called elections for November 29.

In these elections, the overseas vote may be decisive, as Violeta Alonso, Pedro Sánchez's liaison for the Grandchildren's Law abroad, acknowledged this week by urging people to vote , stating that if Spanish citizens residing abroad and those naturalized under the Grandchildren's Law mobilize, it will have a "significant impact" on the elections.

SECTION 6 CORPORATE PROFILE

6.1 Activities

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V., a leading telecommunications provider headquartered in Mexico, operates across Latin America, including Mexico, Central and South America, and the Caribbean. The company specializes in mobile and fixed-line telephony, broadband internet, pay television, and related digital services, serving over 280 million customers through its extensive network infrastructure. Its core business revolves around delivering wireless communication, high-speed data connectivity, and entertainment solutions, with a strong emphasis on innovation in 5G technology and fiber-optic expansions. The fastest-growing segments include mobile data services, driven by rising smartphone adoption and demand for streaming content, as well as broadband offerings through fiber-to-the-home deployments, which have seen significant expansion in urban and emerging markets. This strategic focus has positioned America Movil as a key player in bridging the digital divide, fostering economic growth in the regions it serves. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 3rd largest Telecommunication company by market capitalization.

SECTION 6 CORPORATE PROFILE

6.1 Activities

Fomento Económico Mexicana S.A.B. de C.V. (FEMSA), a Monterrey, Mexico-based multinational conglomerate, is primarily engaged in the production, bottling, and distribution of beverages through its Coca-Cola FEMSA subsidiary, which operates as one of the world's largest Coca-Cola franchisees. The company also manages a vast retail network, including the OXXO convenience store chain, which dominates Mexico's retail landscape and extends into select international markets. Additionally, FEMSA operates in logistics, fuel retailing, and health sciences. The fastest-growing segments include retail, driven by the aggressive expansion of OXXO stores and digital initiatives that enhance customer convenience, as well as beverage operations in emerging markets, fueled by rising consumer demand for non-alcoholic drinks and strategic acquisitions. This diversified approach has positioned FEMSA as a resilient player in the global consumer goods sector, emphasizing innovation and sustainability. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 5th largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

Fomento Económico Mexicana S.A.B. de C.V. (FEMSA), a Monterrey, Mexico-based multinational conglomerate, is primarily engaged in the production, bottling, and distribution of beverages through its Coca-Cola FEMSA subsidiary, which operates as one of the world's largest Coca-Cola franchisees. The company also manages a vast retail network, including the OXXO convenience store chain, which dominates Mexico's retail landscape and extends into select international markets. Additionally, FEMSA operates in logistics, fuel retailing, and health sciences. The fastest-growing segments include retail, driven by the aggressive expansion of OXXO stores and digital initiatives that enhance customer convenience, as well as beverage operations in emerging markets, fueled by rising consumer demand for non-alcoholic drinks and strategic acquisitions. This diversified approach has positioned FEMSA as a resilient player in the global consumer goods sector, emphasizing innovation and sustainability. lseg:urn:newsml:newsroom:20261104:nNRA2k.html_limpio: Los cambios en las deducciones del impuesto sobre la renta (ISR) y las modificaciones a las pérdidas fiscales aprobadas por el Congreso de la Unión afectarán las finanzas de Grupo Financiero Banorte, resultando en un aumento en los pagos de impuestos, según su CEO, José Marcos Ramírez Miguel. Banorte pagó 17.407 millones de pesos en impuestos entre enero y septiembre, un incremento anual del 11%. A partir del 1 de enero de 2027, el Servicio de Administración Tributaria (SAT) limitará las deducciones corporativas a un máximo del 96.67% del ingreso gravable, con el objetivo de evitar que las empresas reduzcan artificialmente su base gravable. Además, se aprobó un límite en la amortización de pérdidas fiscales al 50% de la utilidad fiscal. Ramírez Miguel también destacó el impacto que este nuevo marco fiscal tendrá en los clientes de Banorte, indicando que se evaluará su capacidad crediticia bajo las nuevas reglas. En cuanto a la Ley de Economía Digital, el CEO la considera positiva para la inclusión financiera, esperando su publicación para que el Ministerio de Hacienda defina los sectores clave que solo aceptarán pagos electrónicos. Al cierre del tercer trimestre, los depósitos tradicionales de Banorte crecieron un 13% anual, alcanzando 1.24 billones de pesos, y la utilidad neta del grupo fue de 15.658 millones de pesos, un aumento del 20% anual.

Banorte pagó 17.407 millones de pesos en impuestos entre enero y septiembre, un incremento anual del 11%. A partir del 1 de enero de 2027, el Servicio de Administración Tributaria (SAT) limitará las deducciones corporativas a un máximo del 96.67% del ingreso gravable, con el objetivo de evitar que las empresas reduzcan artificialmente su base gravable. Además, se aprobó un límite en la amortización de pérdidas fiscales al 50% de la utilidad fiscal. Ramírez Miguel también destacó el impacto que este nuevo marco fiscal tendrá en los clientes de Banorte, indicando que se evaluará su capacidad crediticia bajo las nuevas reglas. En cuanto a la Ley de Economía Digital, el CEO la considera positiva para la inclusión financiera, esperando su publicación para que el Ministerio de Hacienda defina los sectores clave que solo aceptarán pagos electrónicos. Al cierre del tercer trimestre, los depósitos tradicionales de Banorte crecieron un 13% anual, alcanzando 1.24 billones de pesos, y la utilidad neta del grupo fue de 15.658 millones de pesos, un aumento del 20% anual.

lseg:urn:newsml:newsroom:20261104:nNRA2k.html_limpio:
Changes to income tax (ISR) deductions, as well as modifications to tax losses approved by the Congress of the Union, will indeed have an impact on the finances of Grupo Financiero Banorte, resulting in higher tax payments, according to its CEO, José Marcos Ramírez Miguel.

"We already have a fiscal impact that we are going to measure carefully and budget for next year when we prepare the budget. We believe that no one likes new taxes, but it will not substantially affect the financial group." The SAT will monitor corporate deductions.

Information from the group, reported to the Mexican Stock Exchange, indicated that between January and September, they paid 17.407 billion pesos in taxes, representing an annual increase of 11%. Starting January 1, 2027, the Tax Administration Service (SAT) will ensure that companies do not deduct more than 96.67% of their taxable income, allowing them to apply 99% of those deductions. However, if they exceed this threshold, the maximum deduction will be equivalent to 96.67% of taxable income. This mechanism aims to prevent companies from artificially reducing their taxable base and thus paying less ISR. The measure is also expected to combat fraudulent billing companies. Another change approved by Congress is the limit on the amortization of tax losses to 50% of fiscal profit. In addition to anticipating a higher tax burden in 2027, José Marcos Ramírez Miguel noted the burden the new fiscal framework regarding ISR will represent for Banorte's clients. "We are looking at which clients and segments could be affected, so we can support them through the process and assess their credit capacity under the new rules," he stated.

Banorte optimistic about the Digital Economy Law

During the press conference, the approval of the Digital Economy Law for Digital and Electronic Payments was also addressed. For Banorte's CEO, the new legal framework is viewed positively for financial inclusion. "(The Digital Economy Law) is a step that the country must take and we gradually need to engage in financial inclusion. I don't believe it will happen all at once, but we all need to aim in that direction, and it's a win-win for those moving money and for the speed at which the economy operates," he said. At this time, the only expectation is that the Digital Economy Law will be published in the Official Gazette of the Federation so that the Ministry of Finance can decide within 15 days which key sectors will only accept payments via card, transfer, or QR codes.

Banorte's profits grow by 20%

At the close of the third quarter, Banorte's traditional deposits grew by 13% annually, amounting to 1.24 trillion pesos. The balance of the Stage 1 and Stage 2 portfolio stood at 1.33 trillion pesos, an annual increase of 11%. In the reported period, the group's net income reached 15.658 billion pesos, an annual increase of 20%.

Jul 06, 2026: America Movil ADR: A Gateway to Latin America's Telecom Expansion

America Movil (Class L ADR) offers investors a significant opportunity to tap into one of Latin America's largest telecom groups, providing extensive exposure to mobile, fixed-line, and broadband services across multiple markets. As of the 6th of July, 2026, the ADR allows US investors to participate in the company's operations through a New York-listed instrument that tracks its Class L shares in Mexico.

With a robust telecom footprint, America Movil operates various segments across Latin America, including mobile voice, data services, broadband internet, and fixed-line connectivity for both residential and business clients. The company has systematically expanded its market presence by investing in mobile networks, acquiring spectrum, and enhancing its service offerings in response to growing data consumption across key regions.

The ADR structure provides a simplified investment pathway for US investors, allowing them to engage with America Movil's performance via a depositary receipt rather than needing to purchase shares directly in the local market. This arrangement not only facilitates smoother currency conversions but also streamlines custody for US-based investment portfolios, making it an attractive option for those looking to diversify their holdings.

America Movil's core business model revolves around delivering diverse connectivity and related services to a wide-ranging customer base across several Latin American countries, often under well-established local brands. Its portfolio includes various offerings, from prepaid mobile plans to bundled broadband packages and digital services catering to the rising demand for streaming, cloud solutions, and enterprise connectivity.

Trading in US dollars, the America Movil Class L ADR presents a compelling opportunity for investors seeking exposure to an influential emerging-markets telecom group. The stock's pricing and liquidity reflect both the performance of its Latin American operations and the broader market sentiment surrounding telecommunications and emerging markets as an asset class, positioning America Movil as a noteworthy option for potential investors.

Jun 22, 2026: America Movil's Claro Box TV: A New Era for 4K Streaming

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its latest innovation, the Claro Box TV, which transforms any HDMI screen into a 4K streaming hub. This compact device, launched on 22nd June 2026, provides seamless access to popular platforms such as Claro Video, Netflix, and YouTube, all navigable via a lightweight, voice-capable remote control.

Claro Box TV is designed for broadband customers in Latin America, offering a convergence of pay TV channels and major streaming apps within a single HDMI device. The system operates on a customized Android TV interface, allowing users to download additional applications from the Google Play Store, including Disney+, Prime Video, and Spotify, alongside pre-installed offerings like Claro Video and YouTube.

Installation is user-friendly; users simply connect one cable to their router and another to their TV, with Wi-Fi connectivity available for those who prefer it. The Bluetooth remote is equipped with dedicated buttons for Netflix and Claro Video, and features voice search capabilities via Google Assistant, contributing to an intuitive user experience.

America Movil's Claro Box TV aims to bolster its broadband customer retention strategy by integrating traditional TV channels with streaming capabilities in a single interface. This approach is particularly beneficial in markets such as Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, where the box not only provides access to live channels but also offers an electronic program guide, minimizing the need to switch inputs during viewing.

As America Movil continues to expand its reach, the Claro Box TV serves as a strategic asset in reducing customer churn in fixed-line broadband services. By controlling both the network and the viewing interface, America Movil can promote its own content alongside partnerships, ensuring a direct relationship with viewers and enhancing its competitive edge in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.

Recent News 3 of 4, Source: HourlyBusinessNews

Jun 16, 2026: America Movil Simplifies Offerings with Telcel Max Sin Limite Plan

America Movil's Telcel Max Sin Limite postpaid plan remains the group's core mobile product in Mexico, with unlimited voice, data bundles, and included streaming perks. The date of this announcement is 16th June 2026, and it serves as a key window for US investors into how America Movil monetizes higher-value subscribers in its home market.

Telcel continues to leverage its Max Sin Limite postpaid plan family as a central tool for retaining higher-value customers. The plans combine unlimited talk and text across Mexico, the US, and Canada, along with sizable mobile data allowances and bundled app access. Currently, Max Sin Limite packages start at approximately MXN 399 per month, scaling up with larger data allowances and more generous streaming and social media benefits, effectively segmenting the market by usage intensity.

The Max Sin Limite concept is built around unlimited voice and SMS in Mexico, with roaming services in the US and Canada. Each plan offers a monthly high-speed data allowance that varies from single-digit gigabytes to significantly higher volumes for heavy users. Certain apps, including popular social networks, do not count toward the primary data bucket or come with additional dedicated data, making the plans more attractive for customers who consistently use these services. This strategy ties the commercial offer to America Movil's ongoing investments in mobile infrastructure.

From a customer perspective, the simplicity of a flat-fee structure with unlimited calling across North America reduces bill shock for cross-border workers and frequent travelers, providing predictable monthly costs for connectivity. Higher-end Max Sin Limite tiers also include value-added services such as additional cloud storage and discounts on handset financing, positioning the plans as a comprehensive bundle rather than just a connectivity service. This bundling strategy is vital for America Movil to differentiate Telcel in a competitive Mexican mobile market that includes AT&T and Telefonica's Movistar.

Industry observers note that Telcel's Max Sin Limite offerings align with America Movil's broader convergence push, where mobile, fixed broadband, and pay TV services are increasingly marketed together. The growing fiber footprint in Mexico allows for cross-selling mobile plans to existing fixed-line customers, enhancing revenue per household. Analysts emphasize the importance of postpaid and convergent offerings in stabilizing overall revenue for America Movil, especially as the company expands its 5G coverage and explores new digital services.

May 27, 2026: America Movil Charts Steady Growth Path with $7 Billion Capex Plan

MEXICO CITY - Mexican telecommunications giant America Movil on Wednesday outlined its financial outlook through 2028, targeting steady growth in revenue and core earnings while holding capital expenditure stable at around $7 billion per year. This information was shared during the company's investor day event, which took place on 27th May 2026, in New York.

During the presentation, America Movil projected that its revenue from services will grow by an average of 4.0% to 5.0% each year from 2026 to 2028. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) are expected to increase between 4.5% and 6.0% annually over the same period. The firm believes that a stable capital expenditure plan will support these growth targets.

The Latin American market leader plans to maintain its capital spending at approximately $7 billion per year, totaling $21 billion over the three-year period. Executives noted that this level of investment is feasible as the company has largely completed its significant purchases of radio frequencies necessary for its 5G network rollout.

The stable spending plan is designed to generate substantial cash, which America Movil intends to utilize for acquisitions, debt reduction, and returning value to investors. The company's executives confirmed they are actively seeking acquisition opportunities, particularly among struggling internet providers in Brazil and telecom operators in Eastern Europe, including Serbia and Slovenia.

For key markets like Brazil and Colombia, management expressed an aspiration to 'join the club of 50,' referring to a long-term goal of achieving a 50% profit margin. This ambitious target underscores America Movil's commitment to enhancing its operational efficiency and market position in the competitive telecommunications landscape.

Jul 06, 2026: America Movil ADR: A Gateway to Latin America's Telecom Expansion

America Movil (Class L ADR) offers investors a significant opportunity to tap into one of Latin America's largest telecom groups, providing extensive exposure to mobile, fixed-line, and broadband services across multiple markets. As of the 6th of July, 2026, the ADR allows US investors to participate in the company's operations through a New York-listed instrument that tracks its Class L shares in Mexico.

With a robust telecom footprint, America Movil operates various segments across Latin America, including mobile voice, data services, broadband internet, and fixed-line connectivity for both residential and business clients. The company has systematically expanded its market presence by investing in mobile networks, acquiring spectrum, and enhancing its service offerings in response to growing data consumption across key regions.

The ADR structure provides a simplified investment pathway for US investors, allowing them to engage with America Movil's performance via a depositary receipt rather than needing to purchase shares directly in the local market. This arrangement not only facilitates smoother currency conversions but also streamlines custody for US-based investment portfolios, making it an attractive option for those looking to diversify their holdings.

America Movil's core business model revolves around delivering diverse connectivity and related services to a wide-ranging customer base across several Latin American countries, often under well-established local brands. Its portfolio includes various offerings, from prepaid mobile plans to bundled broadband packages and digital services catering to the rising demand for streaming, cloud solutions, and enterprise connectivity.

Trading in US dollars, the America Movil Class L ADR presents a compelling opportunity for investors seeking exposure to an influential emerging-markets telecom group. The stock's pricing and liquidity reflect both the performance of its Latin American operations and the broader market sentiment surrounding telecommunications and emerging markets as an asset class, positioning America Movil as a noteworthy option for potential investors.

Jun 22, 2026: America Movil's Claro Box TV: A New Era for 4K Streaming

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its latest innovation, the Claro Box TV, which transforms any HDMI screen into a 4K streaming hub. This compact device, launched on 22nd June 2026, provides seamless access to popular platforms such as Claro Video, Netflix, and YouTube, all navigable via a lightweight, voice-capable remote control.

Claro Box TV is designed for broadband customers in Latin America, offering a convergence of pay TV channels and major streaming apps within a single HDMI device. The system operates on a customized Android TV interface, allowing users to download additional applications from the Google Play Store, including Disney+, Prime Video, and Spotify, alongside pre-installed offerings like Claro Video and YouTube.

America Movil's Claro Box TV aims to bolster its broadband customer retention strategy by integrating traditional TV channels with streaming capabilities in a single interface. This approach is particularly beneficial in markets such as Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, where the box not only provides access to live channels but also offers an electronic program guide, minimizing the need to switch inputs during viewing.

As America Movil continues to expand its reach, the Claro Box TV serves as a strategic asset in reducing customer churn in fixed-line broadband services. By controlling both the network and the viewing interface, America Movil can promote its own content alongside partnerships, ensuring a direct relationship with viewers and enhancing its competitive edge in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.

Jun 16, 2026: America Movil Simplifies Offerings with Telcel Max Sin Limite Plan

America Movil's Telcel Max Sin Limite postpaid plan remains the group's core mobile product in Mexico, with unlimited voice, data bundles, and included streaming perks. The date of this announcement is 16th June 2026, and it serves as a key window for US investors into how America Movil monetizes higher-value subscribers in its home market.

Telcel continues to leverage its Max Sin Limite postpaid plan family as a central tool for retaining higher-value customers. The plans combine unlimited talk and text across Mexico, the US, and Canada, along with sizable mobile data allowances and bundled app access. Currently, Max Sin Limite packages start at approximately MXN 399 per month, scaling up with larger data allowances and more generous streaming and social media benefits, effectively segmenting the market by usage intensity.

The Max Sin Limite concept is built around unlimited voice and SMS in Mexico, with roaming services in the US and Canada. Each plan offers a monthly high-speed data allowance that varies from single-digit gigabytes to significantly higher volumes for heavy users. Certain apps, including popular social networks, do not count toward the primary data bucket or come with additional dedicated data, making the plans more attractive for customers who consistently use these services. This strategy ties the commercial offer to America Movil's ongoing investments in mobile infrastructure.

From a customer perspective, the simplicity of a flat-fee structure with unlimited calling across North America reduces bill shock for cross-border workers and frequent travelers, providing predictable monthly costs for connectivity. Higher-end Max Sin Limite tiers also include value-added services such as additional cloud storage and discounts on handset financing, positioning the plans as a comprehensive bundle rather than just a connectivity service. This bundling strategy is vital for America Movil to differentiate Telcel in a competitive Mexican mobile market that includes AT&T and Telefonica's Movistar.

Industry observers note that Telcel's Max Sin Limite offerings align with America Movil's broader convergence push, where mobile, fixed broadband, and pay TV services are increasingly marketed together. The growing fiber footprint in Mexico allows for cross-selling mobile plans to existing fixed-line customers, enhancing revenue per household. Analysts emphasize the importance of postpaid and convergent offerings in stabilizing overall revenue for America Movil, especially as the company expands its 5G coverage and explores new digital services.

May 27, 2026: America Movil Charts Steady Growth Path with $7 Billion Capex Plan

MEXICO CITY - Mexican telecommunications giant America Movil on Wednesday outlined its financial outlook through 2028, targeting steady growth in revenue and core earnings while holding capital expenditure stable at around $7 billion per year. This information was shared during the company's investor day event, which took place on 27th May 2026, in New York.

During the presentation, America Movil projected that its revenue from services will grow by an average of 4.0% to 5.0% each year from 2026 to 2028. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) are expected to increase between 4.5% and 6.0% annually over the same period. The firm believes that a stable capital expenditure plan will support these growth targets.

The Latin American market leader plans to maintain its capital spending at approximately $7 billion per year, totaling $21 billion over the three-year period. Executives noted that this level of investment is feasible as the company has largely completed its significant purchases of radio frequencies necessary for its 5G network rollout.

The stable spending plan is designed to generate substantial cash, which America Movil intends to utilize for acquisitions, debt reduction, and returning value to investors. The company's executives confirmed they are actively seeking acquisition opportunities, particularly among struggling internet providers in Brazil and telecom operators in Eastern Europe, including Serbia and Slovenia.

For key markets like Brazil and Colombia, management expressed an aspiration to 'join the club of 50,' referring to a long-term goal of achieving a 50% profit margin. This ambitious target underscores America Movil's commitment to enhancing its operational efficiency and market position in the competitive telecommunications landscape.

Sep 09, 2026: Derek Gaskins Takes Marketing Helm at OXXO USA

Derek Gaskins is set to re-enter the convenience-store sector, joining OXXO USA as vice president of marketing and category management. The move will take effect in mid-September, 2026, specifically on the 13th of that month, as Gaskins confirmed in an interview with CSP Daily News.

In his new position at OXXO USA, a subsidiary of Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. (FEMSA), Gaskins will play a pivotal role in shaping the brand's commercial strategy in the U.S. market. He will report directly to CEO Jaime Longoria and oversee a wide array of functions including marketing, merchandising, foodservice, brand development, and supplier partnerships. Gaskins expressed enthusiasm for the role, stating, 'It's one of the most exciting scopes I've had in my career.'

OXXO, which boasts over 26,000 stores globally, has recently made its foray into the United States, acquiring 249 stores from Delek US in October 2024. As OXXO seeks to build a neighborhood-relevant, food-forward convenience experience, Gaskins is expected to harness his extensive industry experience to drive growth. He noted, 'They are trying to build something meaningful here—and they asked me to help lead that commercial effort.'

Prior to this role, Gaskins held positions at Hotel Chocolat and bp, where he focused on enhancing customer experience and operational efficiency. His background includes significant tenures at various convenience retail brands, positioning him as a seasoned leader in the sector. Gaskins remarked, 'OXXO represents something I could not responsibly say no to,' highlighting the strategic importance of this opportunity.

As OXXO USA prepares to establish a stronger foothold in the U.S., Gaskins emphasized the brand's commitment to earning its place in the market. He noted, 'FEMSA came to stay, and they are bringing global best practices, significant capital, and a proven operating model.' With Gaskins at the helm of marketing, OXXO USA is poised to become a serious contender in the competitive convenience store landscape.

Derek Gaskins is set to re-enter the convenience-store sector, joining OXXO USA as vice president of marketing and category management. The move will take effect in mid-September, 2026, specifically on the 13th of that month, as Gaskins confirmed in an interview with CSP Daily News.

Grupo Financiero Banorte reported on Tuesday a year-over-year growth of 13% in traditional deposits and 11% in its loan portfolio during the third quarter of 2026, despite the impact of the removal of the deductibility of contributions to the Institute for the Protection of Bank Savings (IPAB) and the increase in VAT on insurance.

The institution managed to absorb the fiscal cost through widespread growth in its portfolios and the performance of its banking, Afores, pensions, and insurance businesses.

"The non-deductibility of IPAB contributions affects everyone equally. We are all paying the same, and all of us have seen the same increase. It impacted us, but we offset it with other areas," said Marcos Ramírez Miguel, CEO of Grupo Financiero Banorte.

Traditional deposits reached 1 trillion 244.632 billion pesos, while the loan portfolio totaled 1 trillion 333.332 billion. Quarterly net income increased by 20% year-over-year, amounting to 15.658 billion pesos. Additionally, Banorte launched a campaign to raffle off 75 trucks among customers who open a participating account or increase their balance by at least 10,000 pesos.

By segments, the government portfolio grew by 14%; the commercial by 13%; the corporate by 11%; and the consumer by 9%. The performance of the portfolios allowed the group to maintain a growth outlook close to double digits by the end of 2026.

"We are anticipating that it will be very close to double digits, maybe a little below, maybe a little above," noted Ramírez Miguel.

Regarding the anticipated fiscal changes for 2027, the bank is analyzing which companies and segments might be most affected by the new rules in order to assess their credit capacity and support them throughout the process.

"An important task is that we are looking specifically at which clients and which segments may be most affected, so we can assist them in the process and evaluate each of their credit capacities based on the new rules," added the executive.

The institution clarified that the Economic Package for 2027 does not include a structural tax reform. A broader discussion about tax modifications could take place during the preparation of the 2028 Package.

Formal incorporation efforts for XXI Banorte

In another matter, Fernando Solís Soberón, CEO of Afore and Pensions, reported that Banorte won the bidding by the National Commission of the Retirement Savings System (Consar) to manage the accounting and operational administration of accounts for workers who have not yet chosen a retirement fund administrator. Although the funds will remain under the management of the Bank of Mexico, this award will allow the bank to contact account holders and seek their formal incorporation into Afore XXI Banorte.

The executive explained that the institution will be able to offer them advice, personalized attention, and tools to improve their retirement planning, as well as promote voluntary savings. He added that the gradual increase in employer contributions, as a result of reforms to the pension system, will support resource accumulation and improve the replacement rate at the time of retirement.

"This allows us to reach out to workers and make them our clients so they can obtain better returns, more personalized service, and greater information to manage their financial planning for retirement," said Solís Soberón.

By segments, the government portfolio increased by 14%; the commercial by 13%; the corporate by 11%; and the consumer by 9%.

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle, targeting family consumption in key Mexican markets. This launch, taking place on 23rd June 2026, is a significant step in the company's strategy to enhance the availability of reusable packaging solutions.

The Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle is designed for households that prefer purchasing beverages in bulk while maintaining the option for return and reuse. This innovative format not only aims to reduce packaging waste but also lowers the per-liter cost for consumers, who can return the bottle to local corner stores, which have long embraced returnable formats.

Mariana Rodriguez, product manager at Coca-Cola FEMSA, noted that the bottle features a more pronounced waist and a textured grip, enhancing usability at family gatherings. The design is lighter than traditional glass returnable bottles, making it easier for all family members, including children and seniors, to handle. While glass maintains a nostalgic appeal, the PET format provides a modern balance of convenience and tradition.

Coca-Cola FEMSA's CEO, John Santa Maria, has emphasized the importance of refillable packaging as a core strategy. The new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle aligns with the company's sustainability goals, as using refillable containers can significantly reduce the carbon footprint associated with beverage consumption. This initiative not only supports environmental efforts but also fosters a culture of reuse among consumers.

Initially available in select Mexican markets, the Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle leverages the existing popularity of refillable formats. The pricing structure typically includes a deposit for the bottle, making it economically advantageous for families who purchase large quantities. This strategic move is expected to positively impact Coca-Cola FEMSA's long-term cash flow and shareholder value, as the company continues to adapt to consumer preferences while committing to sustainable practices.

Jun 17, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Leverages Logistics-as-a-Service to Enhance Distribution

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. is quietly enhancing its distribution capabilities through Fomento Economico Mexicano's Logistics-as-a-Service offering. This innovative service transforms FEMSA's robust Coca-Cola delivery network into a third-party logistics solution for brands requiring efficient, temperature-controlled distribution across Mexico. This strategic move was made public on the 17th of June, 2026, and is expected to reshape the logistical landscape in the region.

FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service fundamentally allows third-party brands to access the same warehousing, routing software, and last-mile fleet utilized by Coca-Cola in Mexico and other Latin American markets. Clients can seamlessly integrate into FEMSA's extensive delivery network, which significantly reduces the need for them to establish their own complex logistics operations. This means that consumer goods can be efficiently delivered to over 3 million points of sale, utilizing existing routes that serve thousands of small retail outlets daily.

For brands, especially those in the fast-moving consumer goods sector, this service provides an invaluable shortcut to market penetration. Products delivered alongside Coca-Cola benefit from the established distribution patterns that store owners are accustomed to, thus facilitating easier acceptance and integration into existing supply chains. The service's reach can substantially expedite market entry for new energy drinks or healthcare products, compressing lengthy rollout periods into mere months.

Technological infrastructure underpins this service, with advanced routing algorithms and inventory management tools ensuring efficient operations. FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service also offers clients features such as order tracking and delivery proof without necessitating additional investment in software. This is particularly crucial for pharmaceuticals and health products, where stringent temperature control and delivery reliability are essential.

Logistics-as-a-Service is a strategic component of FEMSA's broader vision to maximize value from its existing infrastructure. Although still a smaller segment compared to its core Coca-Cola bottling and OXXO retail operations, it represents a significant opportunity for growth. Investors should note that while immediate scale may be limited, the long-term potential for operating leverage in this logistics venture aligns with FEMSA's overarching objective of enhancing its distribution capabilities.

Jul 20, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte's Growth Strategy Emphasizes Sustainability and Innovation

In an exclusive interview, Mr. Jose Luis Munoz, Executive Director of Sustainability & Investor Relations at Grupo Financiero Banorte, outlined the bank's strategic position for sustainable growth. The discussion, held on the 20th of July 2026, highlighted Banorte's financial performance amid a dynamic economic landscape and its commitment to fostering long-term sustainability.

Reflecting on Banorte's 125-year legacy, Munoz emphasized that the definition of a strong bank has evolved with changing economic and geopolitical landscapes. 'Resilience has been a hallmark of Banorte's history,' he explained, noting the bank's ability to navigate various challenges, including the rise of fintech competitors and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. This resilience is evident in the bank's growing loan portfolio, particularly in consumer lending, which saw an increase in mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.

The bank's commitment to the SME sector remains a cornerstone of its strategy, with dedicated resources aimed at improving customer interaction and service. Munoz explained that Banorte's extensive branch network, particularly in economically active regions, positions it favorably to cater to the needs of SMEs. The bank's approach to 'hyper-personalisation' through advanced technology and analytics further differentiates it from competitors, allowing for tailored offerings that resonate with customer needs.

Banorte's financial health is underscored by a robust capital adequacy ratio of 20.06%, well above regulatory requirements. Munoz highlighted the importance of maintaining a safety buffer due to the bank's status as a systemic institution without foreign subsidiaries. This focus on capital preservation, coupled with disciplined risk management, has enabled Banorte to sustain its strong liquidity position and support growth initiatives.

Sustainability is woven into the fabric of Banorte's operations, with initiatives such as the commitment to plant one million trees by 2030 and participation in the Task Force on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD). Munoz noted that these efforts not only enhance the bank's sustainability practices but also help clients navigate risks associated with nature and biodiversity. As Banorte continues to expand its influence in the financial sector, its commitment to innovation, customer experience, and sustainable practices positions it as a key player in Mexico's economic development.

Jul 02, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte Strengthens Its Position in Mexico's Banking Sector

Grupo Financiero Banorte continues to position itself as one of Mexico's largest banks, combining a traditional branch network with digital services as it competes for retail and corporate customers in a changing rate and regulatory environment. As of 2nd July 2026, Banorte operates in an environment shaped by domestic interest rates, economic growth, and evolving regulation.

Grupo Financiero Banorte S.A.B. (ISIN MXP370641013) is one of Mexico's largest financial groups, with activities spanning commercial banking, consumer finance, asset management, insurance, and pension funds. As a major lender in the Mexican market, the group plays a central role in financing households and businesses across the country. Its nationwide branch and ATM network supports a wide retail franchise, while its corporate and government banking units provide services to larger clients and public entities.

Management attention at Banorte typically centers on maintaining a balance between growth and risk, especially in areas such as consumer credit, mortgages, and small-business lending. Asset quality indicators, such as non-performing loans and coverage ratios, are closely watched, as they show how well the bank is managing credit risk in its portfolio. Additionally, capital adequacy remains a key concern, with banks expected to hold sufficient capital buffers to absorb potential losses and comply with regulatory requirements.

Banorte has invested in digital channels to complement its traditional branch network, offering online and mobile banking for individuals and businesses. These platforms allow customers to make payments, transfer funds, and apply for products such as credit cards and personal loans without visiting a branch. The ability to migrate more activity to digital channels helps Banorte improve efficiency by reducing operating costs per customer while maintaining or even expanding its customer base.

Banorte's shares are listed in Mexico, providing investors exposure to the country's financial sector through a diversified banking and financial services group. The stock's performance over time reflects local macroeconomic conditions, interest rate trends, and the bank's own profitability and risk management decisions. For equity investors, key variables often include return on equity, cost-to-income ratios, asset growth, and dividend policy, all of which shape how the market values Banorte relative to both domestic peers and international financial groups.

May 07, 2026: Banorte Secures Title of Best Bank in Mexico Again

Grupo Financiero Banorte has been honored for the third consecutive time as the Best Bank in Mexico by Global Finance, a recognition that comes as the bank continues to excel in various performance metrics. This announcement was made on the 7th of May 2026, and it underscores Banorte's impressive growth in assets, profitability, product innovation, and customer engagement.

The awards from Global Finance are based on stringent criteria including asset growth, profitability, and strategic development, assessed by international analysts and consultants in the financial sector. Carlos Hank Gonzalez, Chairman of the Board of Directors at Banorte, expressed pride in the recognition, stating, "This acknowledgment reflects our financial strength and our commitment to delivering hyper-personalized solutions that anticipate the needs of our customers."

Banorte's recognition as the Best Bank in Mexico reinforces its position as a benchmark in the regional banking sector. The bank has made significant strides in technological transformation, enhancing its digital banking capabilities, and ensuring proximity to customers, which has been instrumental in its success. This approach not only caters to current consumer needs but also positions Banorte for future growth.

With a robust network comprising 1,223 branches, over 12,000 ATMs, and a workforce of approximately 35,176 employees, Grupo Financiero Banorte is well-equipped to maintain its competitive edge in the financial services landscape. The bank also integrates various financial services, from brokerage to asset management through Afore XXI Banorte, reinforcing its diverse offerings to both individuals and businesses.

Since its inception in 1987, Global Finance has been a leading publication in the financial sector, providing critical insights to corporate leaders and investors. The recognition of Banorte as the Best Bank in Mexico not only highlights its achievements but also sets a high standard for other financial institutions in Latin America.

Jul 20, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte's Growth Strategy Emphasizes Sustainability and Innovation

In an exclusive interview, Mr. Jose Luis Munoz, Executive Director of Sustainability & Investor Relations at Grupo Financiero Banorte, outlined the bank's strategic position for sustainable growth. The discussion, held on the 20th of July 2026, highlighted Banorte's financial performance amid a dynamic economic landscape and its commitment to fostering long-term sustainability.

Reflecting on Banorte's 125-year legacy, Munoz emphasized that the definition of a strong bank has evolved with changing economic and geopolitical landscapes. 'Resilience has been a hallmark of Banorte's history,' he explained, noting the bank's ability to navigate various challenges, including the rise of fintech competitors and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. This resilience is evident in the bank's growing loan portfolio, particularly in consumer lending, which saw an increase in mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.

The bank's commitment to the SME sector remains a cornerstone of its strategy, with dedicated resources aimed at improving customer interaction and service. Munoz explained that Banorte's extensive branch network, particularly in economically active regions, positions it favorably to cater to the needs of SMEs. The bank's approach to 'hyper-personalisation' through advanced technology and analytics further differentiates it from competitors, allowing for tailored offerings that resonate with customer needs.

Banorte's financial health is underscored by a robust capital adequacy ratio of 20.06%, well above regulatory requirements. Munoz highlighted the importance of maintaining a safety buffer due to the bank's status as a systemic institution without foreign subsidiaries. This focus on capital preservation, coupled with disciplined risk management, has enabled Banorte to sustain its strong liquidity position and support growth initiatives.

Sustainability is woven into the fabric of Banorte's operations, with initiatives such as the commitment to plant one million trees by 2030 and participation in the Task Force on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD). Munoz noted that these efforts not only enhance the bank's sustainability practices but also help clients navigate risks associated with nature and biodiversity. As Banorte continues to expand its influence in the financial sector, its commitment to innovation, customer experience, and sustainable practices positions it as a key player in Mexico's economic development.

Jul 02, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte Strengthens Its Position in Mexico's Banking Sector

Grupo Financiero Banorte continues to position itself as one of Mexico's largest banks, combining a traditional branch network with digital services as it competes for retail and corporate customers in a changing rate and regulatory environment. As of 2nd July 2026, Banorte operates in an environment shaped by domestic interest rates, economic growth, and evolving regulation.

Grupo Financiero Banorte S.A.B. (ISIN MXP370641013) is one of Mexico's largest financial groups, with activities spanning commercial banking, consumer finance, asset management, insurance, and pension funds. As a major lender in the Mexican market, the group plays a central role in financing households and businesses across the country. Its nationwide branch and ATM network supports a wide retail franchise, while its corporate and government banking units provide services to larger clients and public entities.

Management attention at Banorte typically centers on maintaining a balance between growth and risk, especially in areas such as consumer credit, mortgages, and small-business lending. Asset quality indicators, such as non-performing loans and coverage ratios, are closely watched, as they show how well the bank is managing credit risk in its portfolio. Additionally, capital adequacy remains a key concern, with banks expected to hold sufficient capital buffers to absorb potential losses and comply with regulatory requirements.

Banorte has invested in digital channels to complement its traditional branch network, offering online and mobile banking for individuals and businesses. These platforms allow customers to make payments, transfer funds, and apply for products such as credit cards and personal loans without visiting a branch. The ability to migrate more activity to digital channels helps Banorte improve efficiency by reducing operating costs per customer while maintaining or even expanding its customer base.

Banorte's shares are listed in Mexico, providing investors exposure to the country's financial sector through a diversified banking and financial services group. The stock's performance over time reflects local macroeconomic conditions, interest rate trends, and the bank's own profitability and risk management decisions. For equity investors, key variables often include return on equity, cost-to-income ratios, asset growth, and dividend policy, all of which shape how the market values Banorte relative to both domestic peers and international financial groups.

Grupo Financiero Banorte has been honored for the third consecutive time as the Best Bank in Mexico by Global Finance, a recognition that comes as the bank continues to excel in various performance metrics. This announcement was made on the 7th of May 2026, and it underscores Banorte's impressive growth in assets, profitability, product innovation, and customer engagement.

Carlos Hank Gonzalez, Chairman of the Board of Directors at Banorte, expressed pride in the recognition, stating, "This acknowledgment reflects our financial strength and our commitment to delivering hyper-personalized solutions that anticipate the needs of our customers."

Banorte's recognition as the Best Bank in Mexico reinforces its position as a benchmark in the regional banking sector. The bank has made significant strides in technological transformation, enhancing its digital banking capabilities, and ensuring proximity to customers, which has been instrumental in its success. This approach not only caters to current consumer needs but also positions Banorte for future growth.

With a robust network comprising 1,223 branches, over 12,000 ATMs, and a workforce of approximately 35,176 employees, Grupo Financiero Banorte is well-equipped to maintain its competitive edge in the financial services landscape. The bank also integrates various financial services, from brokerage to asset management through Afore XXI Banorte, reinforcing its diverse offerings to both individuals and businesses.

Since its inception in 1987, Global Finance has been a leading publication in the financial sector, providing critical insights to corporate leaders and investors. The recognition of Banorte as the Best Bank in Mexico not only highlights its achievements but also sets a high standard for other financial institutions in Latin America.

Sep 11, 2026: Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico Secures Ps. 8 Billion Credit for Growth

Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico S.A.B. de C.V. (MX:GAPB) has secured a significant financial boost with bank credit lines totaling Ps. 8,000 million from a consortium of prominent lenders, including Santander, BBVA, HSBC, J.P. Morgan, and Scotiabank. On 14th September 2026, the company announced that these short-term facilities, which have terms ranging from 6 to 12 months and feature a floating rate linked to TIIE de Fondeo plus a modest spread, will provide the necessary liquidity at a relatively low cost.

Of the total financing, approximately Ps. 4,258 million is earmarked for refinancing debt securities that are set to mature in September and October 2026. This strategic move is expected to mitigate rollover risk for Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico, ensuring the company maintains a stable financial footing as it navigates its obligations. The remaining Ps. 3,742 million will be allocated to capital investments under its Master Development Program for Mexican airports, which is crucial for ongoing infrastructure expansion and enhancing the company's competitive stance in the regional airport sector.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico operates twelve airports across Mexico's Pacific region, serving major urban centers such as Guadalajara and Tijuana, as well as key tourist destinations like Puerto Vallarta and Los Cabos. Additionally, the company manages Sangster International Airport in Montego Bay and Norman Manley International Airport in Kingston, further solidifying its presence in Jamaica's aviation market.

The recent analyst consensus on Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico stock remains positive, with a rating of 'Buy' and a price target of Ps. 520.00. This optimistic outlook is backed by the company's strategic initiatives and its focus on infrastructure development, which are anticipated to bolster growth and profitability in the coming years.

Jun 01, 2026: Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico Completes Full Acquisition of Cross Border Xpress

Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico S.A.B. de C.V. (GAP) has successfully finalized its acquisition of Cross Border Xpress, marking a significant milestone in its expansion strategy. The completion of this transaction was officially recorded on 3rd June 2026, following the notarization of a merger agreement that was initially signed on 30th April 2026.

The acquisition involved GAP purchasing the remaining 25 percent stake in Cross Border Xpress, thereby securing full ownership of the facility. This strategic move not only grants GAP complete control over future earnings but also enhances its operational capabilities in the region. Cross Border Xpress operates a unique pedestrian bridge linking a terminal in San Diego, California, directly to Tijuana International Airport, offering a seamless transit experience for ticketed passengers.

By bypassing traditional border crossing queues, the high-traffic facility generates significant revenue, further complementing Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico's existing airport operations in Tijuana. As a leading airport operator, GAP manages 12 airports across Mexico's Pacific region, serving multiple cities and popular tourist destinations. This acquisition aligns with GAP's strategy to bolster its position in the aviation sector.

In addition to its core aeronautical services, Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico diversifies its revenue streams through non-aeronautical activities, which include commercial services such as car parking, shops, hotels, and restaurants. The acquisition of Cross Border Xpress is expected to enhance these non-aeronautical revenue opportunities, with potential expansions in food and beverage services and VIP lounges anticipated.

Overall, the full acquisition of Cross Border Xpress represents a significant growth opportunity for Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico, allowing the company to maximize its operational synergies and enhance its service offerings in the highly competitive airport management sector.

The Mexican convenience store chain Oxxo, owned by Femsa, closed 140 locations during the third quarter of 2026 as part of a review process of its outlet network aimed at prioritizing the profitability of the business.

In the latest conference with analysts, Femsa's CEO, José Antonio Fernández, explained that the closures are related to older, underperforming stores and are part of a broader optimization process involving approximately 250 establishments.

"We believe it is healthy to periodically review our network of stores and prioritize the long-term profitability of the business ," stated the executive, who indicated they expect to complete the process during the fourth quarter.

The closures had an impact of approximately 20 basis points on Oxxo Mexico's operating margin, Fernández detailed. Excluding these closures, operating profit would have grown by about 8% during the quarter, compared to the 5.8% increase reported by the company.

Between January and September, Oxxo added 462 net stores in Mexico, reaching a total of 24,759 establishments by the end of the period.

In this context, Femsa's Chief Financial Officer, Martín Arias, acknowledged that " we will probably fall somewhat short of our annual target of 1,000 net new stores ." However, he clarified that this is an exception and that the goal remains for 2027 and subsequent years.

Fernández explained that the company started opening new locations later than in previous years due to efforts to improve productivity. "We began our expansion, perhaps a bit later than usual in other years, which has coincided with a process of reducing the number of stores " , said the executive.

On another note, Femsa reported that comparable store sales at Oxxo Mexico increased by 9.2% during the third quarter, driven by a 5.5% rise in average ticket size and a 3.5% increase in customer traffic.

YOU MAY BE INTERESTED

Regional Outlook

Outside of Mexico, Femsa also addressed the situation of Oxxo in Latin America, particularly highlighting growth opportunities in Colombia.

"We are very excited about Colombia," Fernández stated. In this regard, the executive affirmed that the business in that country "is already where we needed it to be" and that the company must accelerate its expansion as much as possible, without compromising the quality of the new stores.

In contrast, he noted that Brazil is still not at that stage, despite the potential observed in that market . Fernández maintained that the company is being "much more prudent" in its expansion while seeking to adapt to the operational restrictions in the country.

Despite this, he expressed confidence in the growth opportunities presented by the Sao Paulo region and stated that the company projects to open approximately 70 net new stores next year.

The Colombian foreign exchange market begins operations on Tuesday, November 3, marked by the official Representative Market Rate set at $3,182.99.

The trading session opens following the holiday on Monday, leaving four working days in which the exchange rate of the US dollar will be influenced by recent monetary policy decisions at both the local and international levels.

During the last week of October, the dollar accumulated an increase of $24.56. This movement contrasts with the downward trend of over 5% recorded throughout the month of October.

Additionally, in the official records from October 3, the Representative Market Rate was positioned at $3,166.91, down from $3,162.35 the previous day. In the online market indicators, the dollar price registers a value of $3,227, with a variation of +0.8%.

For the current week, foreign exchange market estimates presented by Daniel Londoño Tapia, Country Manager of Global66, project that the currency will operate within a trading range of $316 to $325. Similarly, an upward trend is anticipated for this Tuesday, placing the currency near the upper end of the estimated range.

The behavior of the exchange rate is influenced, internally, by the decision of the Board of Directors of the Bank of the Republic to maintain the intervention interest rate at 12.25%. The vote within the issuing body was divided, with four votes in favor of keeping the rate steady and three in favor of a 25-basis-point increase, unlike the increase to 12.5% anticipated by market analysts.

This measure is complemented by the announcement from the Bank regarding a direct purchase of US$2 million from the national government before the year's end, aimed at adjusting international reserves to the levels recommended by the International Monetary Fund.

Since this is a direct transaction outside the foreign exchange market, these funds do not enter the local dollar supply. The central bank's agenda includes the publication of the Monetary Policy Report on Wednesday, the Board's minutes on Thursday, and the presentation of the report on Friday, alongside the initiation of the Economic Rescue Bill in Congress.

In the external environment, the US Federal Reserve maintained its interest rate in the range of 3.75% to 4%.

The US market is focusing on the midterm elections scheduled for Tuesday, November 3, and the October employment report expected on Friday, November 6. Currently, there is a 75% probability of a rate increase by the Fed in December.

Moreover, global risk aversion is influenced by geopolitical warnings from Washington regarding potential military operations against Iran in the Gulf, while the Brent crude oil reference has shifted to the January contract, trading about US$4 below the previous contract. In other indicators, the Euro is valued at $3,597.9, the loan shark rate in Colombia is at 28.34%, coffee is at US$294.5, and gold is at US$3,939.69.
