Press Release article 3 of 5, Source: WEC, 313 words

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

Press Release article 4 of 5, Source: WEC, 182 words

Nov 06, 2025: ASUR Announces Total Passenger Traffic for October 2025

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR), ASUR, a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the U.S. and Colombia, today announced that passenger traffic for October 2025 reached a total of 5.3 million passengers, representing an increase of 1.0% compared to October 2024. Passenger traffic increased 5.1% year-on-year in Colombia, while it presented declines of 0.2% in Mexico and 1.7% in Puerto Rico. Passenger traffic growth in Colombia was driven by increases of 14.8% in international traffic and 2.5% in domestic traffic. Mexico reported a 0.5% decrease in domestic traffic nearly offset by a 0.1% increase in international traffic. Puerto Rico reported an increase of 10.8% in international traffic more than offset by a decrease of 3.6% in domestic traffic. All figures in this statement reflect comparisons between the period from October 1 to 31, 2025 and from October 1 to 31, 2024. Figures excluded transit and general aviation passengers for Mexico and Colombia.

Source: Company Website

Press Release article 5 of 5, Source: WEC, 118 words

Nov 05, 2025: ASUR Announces at the request of the Mexican Stock Exchange ("BMV")

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR), ASUR, a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the U.S. and Colombia, at the request of the Mexican Stock Exchange ("BMV") and in compliance with article 50 of the provisions applicable to securities issuers ("Circular Unica de Emisoras"), confirms that it has submitted an offer to Motiva Infraestructura de Mobilidade S.A. ("Motiva") for its participation in their airports of Brazil, Ecuador, Curacao, and Costa Rica. As of today, no agreements have been signed with the exception of the submitted offer.

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

Nov 06, 2025: ASUR Announces Total Passenger Traffic for October 2025

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR), ASUR, a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the U.S. and Colombia, today announced that passenger traffic for October 2025 reached a total of 5.3 million passengers, representing an increase of 1.0% compared to October 2024. Passenger traffic increased 5.1% year-on-year in Colombia, while it presented declines of 0.2% in Mexico and 1.7% in Puerto Rico. Passenger traffic growth in Colombia was driven by increases of 14.8% in international traffic and 2.5% in domestic traffic. Mexico reported a 0.5% decrease in domestic traffic nearly offset by a 0.1% increase in international traffic. Puerto Rico reported an increase of 10.8% in international traffic more than offset by a decrease of 3.6% in domestic traffic. All figures in this statement reflect comparisons between the period from October 1 to 31, 2025 and from October 1 to 31, 2024. Figures excluded transit and general aviation passengers for Mexico and Colombia.

Press Release article 3 of 5, Source: WEC, 313 words

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

Press Release article 4 of 5, Source: WEC, 182 words

Nov 06, 2025: ASUR Announces Total Passenger Traffic for October 2025

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR), ASUR, a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the U.S. and Colombia, today announced that passenger traffic for October 2025 reached a total of 5.3 million passengers, representing an increase of 1.0% compared to October 2024. Passenger traffic increased 5.1% year-on-year in Colombia, while it presented declines of 0.2% in Mexico and 1.7% in Puerto Rico. Passenger traffic growth in Colombia was driven by increases of 14.8% in international traffic and 2.5% in domestic traffic. Mexico reported a 0.5% decrease in domestic traffic nearly offset by a 0.1% increase in international traffic. Puerto Rico reported an increase of 10.8% in international traffic more than offset by a decrease of 3.6% in domestic traffic. All figures in this statement reflect comparisons between the period from October 1 to 31, 2025 and from October 1 to 31, 2024. Figures excluded transit and general aviation passengers for Mexico and Colombia.

SECTION 8 CORPORATE PROFILE

8.1 Activities

Kimberly-Clark de Mexico S.A. de C.V., a subsidiary of the global Kimberly-Clark Corporation, is a leading manufacturer and marketer of personal care and consumer tissue products in Mexico. The company specializes in producing a diverse portfolio of essential items, including baby diapers, feminine hygiene products, facial tissues, toilet paper, and professional wipes for healthcare and industrial applications. Its operations emphasize innovation, sustainability, and efficient supply chain management to serve both domestic and international markets. Among its fastest-growing segments are premium personal care products, such as advanced incontinence and feminine care solutions, fueled by rising consumer demand for high-quality, eco-friendly options and expanding e-commerce channels. Additionally, the professional segment, particularly wipes and protective gear, has seen strong growth due to increased adoption in healthcare and workplace safety sectors, positioning the company for continued market expansion in Latin America. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 19th largest Health care company by market capitalization.

Kimberly-Clark de Mexico S.A. de C.V., a subsidiary of the global Kimberly-Clark Corporation, is a leading manufacturer and marketer of personal care and consumer tissue products in Mexico. Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. (KOF) is emerging as a potentially undervalued opportunity in the consumer staples sector. As of 9th July 2026, the company stands as the largest Coca-Cola bottler worldwide by sales volume, serving over 270 million consumers throughout Latin America with a diverse product range that includes sparkling beverages, water, juices, sports drinks, and dairy products.

Despite operating in a mature and competitive consumer staples industry, Coca-Cola FEMSA's current market valuation suggests that investors may be overlooking its resilient cash flows and strong profitability. The firm maintains a strong free cash flow of about MXN 24.2 billion, showcasing its capability to support dividends, investments, and strategic acquisitions.

The company's financial health is further illustrated by its balance sheet, which lists total assets at approximately MXN 314.5 billion and total liabilities at around MXN 160.5 billion, resulting in a solid shareholders' equity of about MXN 154.0 billion. Despite slight increases in leverage due to acquisitions, Coca-Cola FEMSA continues to exhibit strong cash generation, enabling it to navigate macroeconomic challenges such as currency volatility and inflation.

While market concerns such as slowing consumer spending and rising commodity costs persist, Coca-Cola FEMSA's fundamentals remain compelling. Jul 05, 2026: Coca-Cola Femsa Expands Beverage Operations for Long-Term Growth

Coca-Cola Femsa S.A.B. de C.V., the largest Coca-Cola bottler in the world by volume, continues to leverage its wide Latin American footprint and franchise agreements to drive beverage distribution and long-term growth opportunities. As of the 5th of July, 2026, Coca-Cola Femsa's operations underline a robust business model focused on efficiency and localized strategies that resonate with regional consumer preferences.

Coca-Cola Femsa oversees a broad network of bottling plants and distribution centers that support a high-frequency, high-volume beverage business in both emerging and developed Latin American economies. Its territories include key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, and other countries in Central and South America, where population density and urbanization provide a large consumer base for ready-to-drink beverages. The company manages operations spanning manufacturing, warehousing, logistics, and last-mile delivery to retailers, restaurants, and other points of sale.

The company operates under long-term franchise and bottling agreements that define its rights and obligations to produce, market, and sell Coca-Cola branded beverages in assigned territories. Within this framework, Coca-Cola Femsa focuses on operational efficiency, portfolio management, and local commercial strategies while coordinating with the brand owner on marketing and innovation. This strategic approach allows the company to combine globally recognized brands with local knowledge of consumer preferences and retail formats.

Beyond classic colas, Coca-Cola Femsa manages a broad beverage portfolio that typically includes flavored sparkling soft drinks, still juices, sports drinks, teas, and bottled water. The company adapts flavors, package sizes, and multipack configurations to local consumer tastes and price points, ensuring a tailored approach that meets diverse market demands. Packaging innovation plays a central role in Coca-Cola Femsa's operations, as the company strives to meet sustainability expectations and improve efficiency.

From an investor perspective, Coca-Cola Femsa is often viewed as a consumer staples business with exposure to multiple Latin American currencies and macroeconomic environments. Analysts closely monitor capital expenditure commitments, leverage metrics, and dividend policies when assessing the balance between growth investment and shareholder returns. For many global investors, Coca-Cola Femsa represents an opportunity to tap into Latin American consumer trends through a well-established beverage platform tied to iconic soft drink brands.

Jun 23, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Launches 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle to Enhance Family Consumption

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle, targeting family consumption in key Mexican markets. This launch, taking place on 23rd June 2026, is a significant step in the company's strategy to enhance the availability of reusable packaging solutions.

The Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle is designed for households that prefer purchasing beverages in bulk while maintaining the option for return and reuse. This innovative format not only aims to reduce packaging waste but also lowers the per-liter cost for consumers, who can return the bottle to local corner stores, which have long embraced returnable formats.

Mariana Rodriguez, product manager at Coca-Cola FEMSA, noted that the bottle features a more pronounced waist and a textured grip, enhancing usability at family gatherings. The design is lighter than traditional glass returnable bottles, making it easier for all family members, including children and seniors, to handle. While glass maintains a nostalgic appeal, the PET format provides a modern balance of convenience and tradition.

Coca-Cola FEMSA's CEO, John Santa Maria, has emphasized the importance of refillable packaging as a core strategy. The new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle aligns with the company's sustainability goals, as using refillable containers can significantly reduce the carbon footprint associated with beverage consumption. This initiative not only supports environmental efforts but also fosters a culture of reuse among consumers.

Initially available in select Mexican markets, the Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle leverages the existing popularity of refillable formats. The pricing structure typically includes a deposit for the bottle, making it economically advantageous for families who purchase large quantities. This strategic move is expected to positively impact Coca-Cola FEMSA's long-term cash flow and shareholder value, as the company continues to adapt to consumer preferences while committing to sustainable practices.

Jun 17, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Leverages Logistics-as-a-Service to Enhance Distribution

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. is quietly enhancing its distribution capabilities through Fomento Economico Mexicano's Logistics-as-a-Service offering. This innovative service transforms FEMSA's robust Coca-Cola delivery network into a third-party logistics solution for brands requiring efficient, temperature-controlled distribution across Mexico. This strategic move was made public on the 17th of June, 2026, and is expected to reshape the logistical landscape in the region.

FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service fundamentally allows third-party brands to access the same warehousing, routing software, and last-mile fleet utilized by Coca-Cola in Mexico and other Latin American markets. Clients can seamlessly integrate into FEMSA's extensive delivery network, which significantly reduces the need for them to establish their own complex logistics operations. This means that consumer goods can be efficiently delivered to over 3 million points of sale, utilizing existing routes that serve thousands of small retail outlets daily.

For brands, especially those in the fast-moving consumer goods sector, this service provides an invaluable shortcut to market penetration. Products delivered alongside Coca-Cola benefit from the established distribution patterns that store owners are accustomed to, thus facilitating easier acceptance and integration into existing supply chains. The service's reach can substantially expedite market entry for new energy drinks or healthcare products, compressing lengthy rollout periods into mere months.

Technological infrastructure underpins this service, with advanced routing algorithms and inventory management tools ensuring efficient operations. FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service also offers clients features such as order tracking and delivery proof without necessitating additional investment in software. This is particularly crucial for pharmaceuticals and health products, where stringent temperature control and delivery reliability are essential.

Logistics-as-a-Service is a strategic component of FEMSA's broader vision to maximize value from its existing infrastructure. Although still a smaller segment compared to its core Coca-Cola bottling and OXXO retail operations, it represents a significant opportunity for growth. Investors should note that while immediate scale may be limited, the long-term potential for operating leverage in this logistics venture aligns with FEMSA's overarching objective of enhancing its distribution capabilities.

Jun 17, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Leverages Logistics-as-a-Service to Enhance Distribution

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. is quietly enhancing its distribution capabilities through Fomento Economico Mexicano's Logistics-as-a-Service offering. This strategic move was made public on the 17th of June, 2026, and is expected to reshape the logistical landscape in the region.

For brands, especially those in the fast-moving consumer goods sector, this service provides an invaluable shortcut to market penetration. Products delivered alongside Coca-Cola benefit from the established distribution patterns that store owners are accustomed to, thus facilitating easier acceptance and integration into existing supply chains. The service's reach can substantially expedite market entry for new energy drinks or healthcare products, compressing lengthy rollout periods into mere months.

Technological infrastructure underpins this service, with advanced routing algorithms and inventory management tools ensuring efficient operations. FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service also offers clients features such as order tracking and delivery proof without necessitating additional investment in software. This is particularly crucial for pharmaceuticals and health products, where stringent temperature control and delivery reliability are essential.

Logistics-as-a-Service is a strategic component of FEMSA's broader vision to maximize value from its existing infrastructure. Although still a smaller segment compared to its core Coca-Cola bottling and OXXO retail operations, it represents a significant opportunity for growth. Investors should note that while immediate scale may be limited, the long-term potential for operating leverage in this logistics venture aligns with FEMSA's overarching objective of enhancing its distribution capabilities.

SECTION 8 CORPORATE PROFILE

8.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Jun 16, 2026: Walmart's New Braunfels Distribution Center to Undergo $8M Automation Upgrade

Walmart is set to initiate a significant renovation of its distribution center in New Braunfels, Texas, with a budget of $8 million. The project is scheduled to commence on August 17, 2026, and is expected to be completed by September 17, 2027. This renovation phase will focus on selective demolition, the installation of new electrical systems, enhanced material-handling equipment, and upgrades to fire suppression and compressed air systems, as detailed in a filing with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation.

This ongoing renovation reflects Walmart's broader strategy to automate its distribution network and optimize operational costs. The retail giant has identified automation as a crucial element in managing its primary cost drivers: inventory and labor. Earlier this year, Walmart executives highlighted that capital spending on supply chain improvements is likely to peak in the coming years, with automation accounting for a significant share of this investment. Currently, Walmart is upgrading 23 of its 42 regional distribution centers with advanced automation technology, with plans to eventually modernize all facilities in its network.

Walmart has previously indicated that automation contributes to reduced shipping costs by improving operational efficiency. Presently, more than 60% of the retailer's U.S. locations receive goods from automated distribution centers. This strategic move towards automation is designed to enhance efficiency across Walmart's supply chain, allowing the company to respond more effectively to changing market demands.

While Walmart did not provide additional details about the New Braunfels project, the investment aligns with the company's goal of streamlining its distribution processes. As Walmart continues to modernize its operations, it is likely to maintain its competitive edge in an increasingly automated retail landscape. The commitment to upgrading the New Braunfels facility underscores Walmart's focus on leveraging technology to drive growth and operational excellence.

As Walmart embarks on this $8 million renovation, stakeholders and investors will be closely monitoring the outcomes of its automation initiatives. The New Braunfels distribution center's remodel may serve as a bellwether for Walmart's future investments in technology-driven efficiencies, reinforcing the company's position as a leader in the retail sector.

Walmart Inc. (NYSE: WMT) is accelerating its global e-commerce push with a string of moves designed to expand reach and speed up fulfillment for customers worldwide. On 11th June 2026, the retail giant opened Walmart.com to customers in Mexico, granting access to hundreds of thousands of eligible items spanning apparel, home goods, electronics, and more.

This international expansion marks a significant shift in how Walmart approaches its online marketplace, moving well beyond its traditional domestic pickup and delivery model. Duties, taxes, and fees are displayed at checkout for cross-border orders, giving Mexican customers full pricing transparency before completing their purchases. Walmart has also confirmed plans to extend international shipping to additional markets in the future, signaling that the Mexico launch is just the first step in a broader global strategy.

On the domestic front, Walmart announced on 28th May that 30-minute-or-less delivery is now available across 33 U.S. markets, covering more than 100,000 eligible items. Products available for rapid delivery include groceries, pharmacy items, household supplies, pet food, electronics, and prescriptions, making the service broadly useful for everyday shopping needs.

In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Walmart reported that global e-commerce grew 26%, with Walmart U.S. e-commerce and Walmart International e-commerce growing 26% and 27% respectively. Store-fulfilled delivery has more than doubled over the past two years, with more than 36% of U.S. orders in the quarter delivered in under three hours.

The combination of rapid domestic delivery and expanding international access positions Walmart as a formidable competitor in the global e-commerce landscape, challenging pure-play online retailers on multiple fronts. With international shipping infrastructure now taking shape and domestic fulfillment networks continuing to mature, Walmart appears well-positioned to sustain its e-commerce momentum through the remainder of fiscal 2027.

May 26, 2026: Walmart's New Prepaid Consolidation Program Aims to Boost Delivery Efficiency

Walmart has introduced a program designed to streamline inbound supplier logistics, according to a news release on Tuesday. The initiative, called the Prepaid Consolidation Program, aims to accelerate product delivery to shelves and customers. The rollout of this program will commence on 26th May 2026.

The Prepaid Consolidation Program allows suppliers to send items under a single national purchase order to one location, rather than dispatching multiple individual orders to various facilities. This consolidation enables Walmart to improve transportation efficiency by redistributing inventory across its 42 regional distribution centers.

The phased rollout will involve supplier participation based on volume alignment and capacity expansion, as stated by Walmart. Suppliers interested in participating can reach out to Walmart or to a designated provider to check their eligibility. The initiative is expected to enhance inventory replenishment accuracy, reduce variability, and support improved in-stock rates at Walmart stores.

Mike Gray, senior vice president of Supply Chain at Walmart U.S., emphasized the company's focus on simplifying and expediting the supply chain for suppliers while ensuring product availability for customers. He noted that enhancing first-mile capabilities reduces complexity and keeps goods moving, ultimately delivering more value.

The program is designed to address existing efficiency issues faced by suppliers, who typically must create individual purchase orders and manage multiple shipments. By allowing suppliers to generate one purchase order linked to a single pallet for one facility, Walmart aims to optimize inventory positioning based on customer demand. Furthermore, participation does not necessitate changes to suppliers' prepaid freight terms, and they can manage shipments directly through Walmart or approved third-party logistics providers.

Jun 16, 2026: Walmart's New Braunfels Distribution Center to Undergo $8M Automation Upgrade

Walmart is set to initiate a significant renovation of its distribution center in New Braunfels, Texas, with a budget of $8 million. The project is scheduled to commence on August 17, 2026, and is expected to be completed by September 17, 2027. This renovation phase will focus on selective demolition, the installation of new electrical systems, enhanced material-handling equipment, and upgrades to fire suppression and compressed air systems, as detailed in a filing with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation.

This ongoing renovation reflects Walmart's broader strategy to automate its distribution network and optimize operational costs. The retail giant has identified automation as a crucial element in managing its primary cost drivers: inventory and labor. Earlier this year, Walmart executives highlighted that capital spending on supply chain improvements is likely to peak in the coming years, with automation accounting for a significant share of this investment. Currently, Walmart is upgrading 23 of its 42 regional distribution centers with advanced automation technology, with plans to eventually modernize all facilities in its network.

Walmart has previously indicated that automation contributes to reduced shipping costs by improving operational efficiency. Presently, more than 60% of the retailer's U.S. locations receive goods from automated distribution centers. This strategic move towards automation is designed to enhance efficiency across Walmart's supply chain, allowing the company to respond more effectively to changing market demands.

While Walmart did not provide additional details about the New Braunfels project, the investment aligns with the company's goal of streamlining its distribution processes. As Walmart continues to modernize its operations, it is likely to maintain its competitive edge in an increasingly automated retail landscape. The commitment to upgrading the New Braunfels facility underscores Walmart's focus on leveraging technology to drive growth and operational excellence.

As Walmart embarks on this $8 million renovation, stakeholders and investors will be closely monitoring the outcomes of its automation initiatives. The New Braunfels distribution center's remodel may serve as a bellwether for Walmart's future investments in technology-driven efficiencies, reinforcing the company's position as a leader in the retail sector.

Jun 15, 2026: Walmart (NYSE: WMT) Sets Sights on E-Commerce Growth with Cross-Border Shipping

Walmart Inc. (NYSE: WMT) is accelerating its global e-commerce push with a string of moves designed to expand reach and speed up fulfillment for customers worldwide. On 11th June 2026, the retail giant opened Walmart.com to customers in Mexico, granting access to hundreds of thousands of eligible items spanning apparel, home goods, electronics, and more.

This international expansion marks a significant shift in how Walmart approaches its online marketplace, moving well beyond its traditional domestic pickup and delivery model. Duties, taxes, and fees are displayed at checkout for cross-border orders, giving Mexican customers full pricing transparency before completing their purchases. Walmart has also confirmed plans to extend international shipping to additional markets in the future, signaling that the Mexico launch is just the first step in a broader global strategy.

On the domestic front, Walmart announced on 28th May that 30-minute-or-less delivery is now available across 33 U.S. markets, covering more than 100,000 eligible items. Products available for rapid delivery include groceries, pharmacy items, household supplies, pet food, electronics, and prescriptions, making the service broadly useful for everyday shopping needs.

In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Walmart reported that global e-commerce grew 26%, with Walmart U.S. e-commerce and Walmart International e-commerce growing 26% and 27% respectively. Store-fulfilled delivery has more than doubled over the past two years, with more than 36% of U.S. orders in the quarter delivered in under three hours.

The combination of rapid domestic delivery and expanding international access positions Walmart as a formidable competitor in the global e-commerce landscape, challenging pure-play online retailers on multiple fronts. With international shipping infrastructure now taking shape and domestic fulfillment networks continuing to mature, Walmart appears well-positioned to sustain its e-commerce momentum through the remainder of fiscal 2027.

This strategic move aims to enhance the shopping experience for Mexican consumers, allowing them to access a broader selection of products and discover new brands that were previously unavailable through Walmart. Manish Joneja, Senior Vice President of Walmart Marketplace, emphasized the importance of this initiative, stating, "We're focused on making it easy for customers to access an expanded assortment of products. This is a milestone in the evolution of how people access Walmart.com's marketplace assortment around the world, and we're excited to bring it to Mexico first."

Customers in Mexico will now be able to shop from a vast array of eligible items across various categories, including apparel, home goods, electronics, and more. Walmart has assured that orders will be delivered through the same trusted network that serves millions of customers in the United States daily. Shipping and customs clearance will be managed by established international carriers to ensure reliable delivery.

To celebrate the launch, Walmart is offering a limited-time promotion for orders shipping to Mexico, including free shipping on eligible orders of $35 or more. The company has also indicated plans to expand its international shipping capabilities to additional markets in the future, marking a significant step in its global strategy.

Mexico has long been a key international market for Walmart. May 28, 2026: Walmart Partners with Teladoc to Enhance Virtual Care Services

Walmart has announced a strategic partnership with Teladoc Health, bringing the telehealth provider's virtual care services to its Better Care Services platform. As of 29th May 2026, this collaboration aims to enhance the healthcare experience for Walmart customers by providing access to a range of services including virtual urgent care, dermatology, and nutrition consultations.

The newly integrated services allow both insured and cash-pay customers to access Teladoc's offerings at a competitive price of $89 per visit. The virtual urgent care service addresses common health issues such as sinus infections and urinary tract infections, while dermatology consultations promise a diagnosis within 24 hours from board-certified specialists. Additionally, nutrition services will offer personalized consultations for various health concerns, including diabetes management and prenatal nutrition.

Kelly Bliss, President of U.S. Group Health at Teladoc Health, emphasized the convenience of accessing healthcare through Walmart, stating, "Walmart is where millions of Americans already go for everyday needs, and now, getting care from Teladoc Health can be part of that same experience." The collaboration follows an earlier introduction of Teladoc's BetterHelp mental health services on Walmart's platform, further expanding the range of healthcare options available to consumers.

Teladoc Health, which operates the largest nationwide network of virtual care providers, reported a revenue of $614 million for Q1 2026, surpassing projections of $611.36 million. However, the company's earnings per share came in at -$0.36, slightly below the anticipated -$0.3412. The partnership with Walmart aligns with Teladoc's strategy to diversify its service offerings and improve financial performance, as analysts have noted an upward trend in the company's stock outlook amid these developments.

Analyst firms have responded positively to the news, with Jefferies raising its price target for Teladoc Health to $6.00 and BofA Securities increasing its target to $9.00 while maintaining a Buy rating. These adjustments reflect confidence in Teladoc's ability to navigate the evolving healthcare landscape and capitalize on its partnership with Walmart to enhance service delivery and financial stability.

This investment, disclosed on the 27th of May, 2026, underscores the company's strategy to solidify Mexico's position as a key e-commerce and distribution hub amidst the growing demand for digital commerce.

This investment comes at a time when Walmart de Mexico is also planning to open 18 new stores across various municipalities in the State of Mexico between 2026 and 2027. Currently operating over 400 units in the region and contributing approximately 33,000 jobs, Walmart de Mexico is poised to drive further economic growth while aligning with its broader regional investment strategy. The company reported a consolidated revenue of MX$245.02 billion, falling short of the MX$269.96 billion forecast. Barrientos noted the importance of upcoming consumer events, such as the FIFA World Cup and Mexico's annual Hot Sale, as pivotal opportunities to boost sales. As Walmart de Mexico continues to innovate and enhance its logistics infrastructure, its focus on AI and automation positions it well for future growth in an evolving retail landscape.

AvoFresco, the California-based maker of fresh, squeezable guacamole pouches, is expanding into 700 additional Walmart stores – bringing its total Walmart footprint to 3,000 locations nationwide. With more Americans expected to stay home this summer, accessibility to AvoFresco's offerings is more critical than ever.

Shoppers are looking for fresher, more convenient ways to enjoy avocado every day and more consumers than ever will be able to purchase AvoFresco at their local Walmart.'

AvoFresco is backed by a legacy of avocado excellence through its parent company, Calavo Growers Inc., which has been a leader in avocado innovation for over a century. The company prides itself on using the finest hand-picked Hass avocados to create its products. The guacamole is offered in various formats, including squeeze pouches, tubs, and single-serve cups, catering to diverse consumer needs and occasions.

As the trend towards healthier snacking continues to grow, AvoFresco's expansion into Walmart is a strategic move that not only enhances its market presence but also aligns with consumer preferences for fresh and convenient food options. The Mexican Stock Exchange (BMV) ends with gains, while Wall Street indices close mixed, influenced by investor caution in anticipation of the results of the midterm elections in the United States.

The Price and Quotations Index (IPC) closed this Tuesday's session with an increase of 0.52%, reaching 70,143.09 points, according to data from the exchange itself.

Meanwhile, Wall Street indices finished with uneven results:

  • The S&P 500 rose 0.36%, to 7,568.92 points.
  • The Nasdaq Composite gained 0.83%, to 25,372.01 points.
  • The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.38%, to 55,786.72 points.

BMV rises thanks to Volaris

The local stock market closed with gains after remaining inactive in the previous session due to the Day of the Dead celebrations in Mexico. Consequently, the IPC continues its zigzag trend, which has been in place since October 26.

In addition, BMV exceeded the 70,000-point threshold, something not seen since October 21, when it reached 70,249.54 points.

Volaris' shares performed best, rising 8.38% to 12.94 pesos. In contrast, Peñoles shares had the worst performance within the IPC, dropping 3.65% to 734.50 pesos.

Wall Street focuses on U.S. elections

This Tuesday's trading session was marked by the midterm elections in the United States, where Democrats and Republicans will compete for 35 Senate seats and 435 seats in the House of Representatives.

This electoral contest led investors to adopt a cautious posture, which negatively impacted the performance of the capital markets in New York.

In the corporate sphere, Apple shares fell 2.15% to $331.04 after reporting revenues of $114.477 billion in the third quarter, representing a year-on-year growth of 11.72%.

The tech giant raised concerns after projecting a gross profit margin of between 45% and 46% for the October-December period, below the 47.9% that the market expected.

Despite this, the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite managed to close in positive territory due to the boost from semiconductor stocks. The top-performing stocks included:

  • AMD, which saw a rise of 3.65% to $483.90.
  • Broadcom, up 3.07% to $332.13.
  • Nvidia, which increased 2.27% to $206.65.

Oil prices on November 3, 2026

Oil prices closed mixed as investors analyze expectations for peace in the U.S.-Iran and Ukraine-Russia conflicts.

The December contract for West Texas Intermediate (WTI) rose 0.25% to $96.71 per barrel. Meanwhile, the January contract for North Sea Brent fell 0.37% to $104.38, according to data from the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE).

On one hand, a spokesperson for the Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that the U.S. and Iran remain committed to dialogue and are considering proposals aimed at resolving their differences.

Additionally, U.S. President Donald Trump announced that he had reached an agreement with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to stop providing $4 billion in funding to the Middle Eastern country.

Furthermore, international media reported that Russia will hold peace talks with Ukraine and the United States in Abu Dhabi from November 10 to 11.

The Mexican Stock Exchange (BMV) ends with gains, while Wall Street indices close mixed, influenced by investor caution in anticipation of the results of the midterm elections in the United States.

The Price and Quotations Index (IPC) closed this Tuesday's session with an increase of 0.52%, reaching 70,143.09 points, according to data from the exchange itself.

Meanwhile, Wall Street indices finished with uneven results:

• The S&P 500 rose 0.36%, to 7,568.92 points.
• The Nasdaq Composite gained 0.83%, to 25,372.01 points.
• The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.38%, to 55,786.72 points.
BMV rises thanks to Volaris

The local stock market closed with gains after remaining inactive in the previous session due to the Day of the Dead celebrations in Mexico. Consequently, the IPC continues its zigzag trend, which has been in place since October 26.

In addition, BMV exceeded the 70,000-point threshold, something not seen since October 21, when it reached 70,249.54 points.

Volaris' shares performed best, rising 8.38% to 12.94 pesos. In contrast, Peñoles shares had the worst performance within the IPC, dropping 3.65% to 734.50 pesos.

Wall Street focuses on U.S. elections

This Tuesday's trading session was marked by the midterm elections in the United States, where Democrats and Republicans will compete for 35 Senate seats and 435 seats in the House of Representatives.

This electoral contest led investors to adopt a cautious posture, which negatively impacted the performance of the capital markets in New York.

In the corporate sphere, Apple shares fell 2.15% to $331.04 after reporting revenues of $114.477 billion in the third quarter, representing a year-on-year growth of 11.72%.

The tech giant raised concerns after projecting a gross profit margin of between 45% and 46% for the October-December period, below the 47.9% that the market expected.

Despite this, the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite managed to close in positive territory due to the boost from semiconductor stocks. The top-performing stocks included:

• AMD, which saw a rise of 3.65% to $483.90.
• Broadcom, up 3.07% to $332.13.
• Nvidia, which increased 2.27% to $206.65.
Oil prices on November 3, 2026

Oil prices closed mixed as investors analyze expectations for peace in the U.S.-Iran and Ukraine-Russia conflicts.

The December contract for West Texas Intermediate (WTI) rose 0.25% to $96.71 per barrel. Meanwhile, the January contract for North Sea Brent fell 0.37% to $104.38, according to data from the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE).

On one hand, a spokesperson for the Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that the U.S. and Iran remain committed to dialogue and are considering proposals aimed at resolving their differences.

Additionally, U.S. President Donald Trump announced that he had reached an agreement with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to stop providing $4 billion in funding to the Middle Eastern country.

Furthermore, international media reported that Russia will hold peace talks with Ukraine and the United States in Abu Dhabi from November 10 to 11.

Jun 16, 2026: Walmart's New Braunfels Distribution Center to Undergo $8M Automation Upgrade

Walmart is set to initiate a significant renovation of its distribution center in New Braunfels, Texas, with a budget of $8 million. The project is scheduled to commence on August 17, 2026, and is expected to be completed by September 17, 2027. This renovation phase will focus on selective demolition, the installation of new electrical systems, enhanced material-handling equipment, and upgrades to fire suppression and compressed air systems, as detailed in a filing with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation.

This ongoing renovation reflects Walmart's broader strategy to automate its distribution network and optimize operational costs. The retail giant has identified automation as a crucial element in managing its primary cost drivers: inventory and labor. Earlier this year, Walmart executives highlighted that capital spending on supply chain improvements is likely to peak in the coming years, with automation accounting for a significant share of this investment. Currently, Walmart is upgrading 23 of its 42 regional distribution centers with advanced automation technology, with plans to eventually modernize all facilities in its network.

Walmart has previously indicated that automation contributes to reduced shipping costs by improving operational efficiency. Presently, more than 60% of the retailer's U.S. locations receive goods from automated distribution centers. This strategic move towards automation is designed to enhance efficiency across Walmart's supply chain, allowing the company to respond more effectively to changing market demands.

While Walmart did not provide additional details about the New Braunfels project, the investment aligns with the company's goal of streamlining its distribution processes. As Walmart continues to modernize its operations, it is likely to maintain its competitive edge in an increasingly automated retail landscape. The commitment to upgrading the New Braunfels facility underscores Walmart's focus on leveraging technology to drive growth and operational excellence.

As Walmart embarks on this $8 million renovation, stakeholders and investors will be closely monitoring the outcomes of its automation initiatives. The New Braunfels distribution center's remodel may serve as a bellwether for Walmart's future investments in technology-driven efficiencies, reinforcing the company's position as a leader in the retail sector.

Jun 15, 2026: Walmart (NYSE: WMT) Sets Sights on E-Commerce Growth with Cross-Border Shipping

Walmart Inc. (NYSE: WMT) is accelerating its global e-commerce push with a string of moves designed to expand reach and speed up fulfillment for customers worldwide. On 11th June 2026, the retail giant opened Walmart.com to customers in Mexico, granting access to hundreds of thousands of eligible items spanning apparel, home goods, electronics, and more.

This international expansion marks a significant shift in how Walmart approaches its online marketplace, moving well beyond its traditional domestic pickup and delivery model. Duties, taxes, and fees are displayed at checkout for cross-border orders, giving Mexican customers full pricing transparency before completing their purchases. Walmart has also confirmed plans to extend international shipping to additional markets in the future, signaling that the Mexico launch is just the first step in a broader global strategy.

On the domestic front, Walmart announced on 28th May that 30-minute-or-less delivery is now available across 33 U.S. markets, covering more than 100,000 eligible items. Products available for rapid delivery include groceries, pharmacy items, household supplies, pet food, electronics, and prescriptions, making the service broadly useful for everyday shopping needs.

In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Walmart reported that global e-commerce grew 26%, with Walmart U.S. e-commerce and Walmart International e-commerce growing 26% and 27% respectively. Store-fulfilled delivery has more than doubled over the past two years, with more than 36% of U.S. orders in the quarter delivered in under three hours.

The combination of rapid domestic delivery and expanding international access positions Walmart as a formidable competitor in the global e-commerce landscape, challenging pure-play online retailers on multiple fronts. With international shipping infrastructure now taking shape and domestic fulfillment networks continuing to mature, Walmart appears well-positioned to sustain its e-commerce momentum through the remainder of fiscal 2027.

Jun 11, 2026: Walmart.com Ventures into Mexico with International Expansion

Retail giant Walmart (WMT) is embarking on a significant international expansion of its Walmart.com service, beginning with Mexico. On 12th June 2026, the company announced that it would be opening its Walmart.com website to international customers, unlocking access to hundreds of thousands of items with shipping available to Mexico.

This strategic move aims to enhance the shopping experience for Mexican consumers, allowing them to access a broader selection of products and discover new brands that were previously unavailable through Walmart. Manish Joneja, Senior Vice President of Walmart Marketplace, emphasized the importance of this initiative, stating, "We're focused on making it easy for customers to access an expanded assortment of products. This is a milestone in the evolution of how people access Walmart.com's marketplace assortment around the world, and we're excited to bring it to Mexico first."

Customers in Mexico will now be able to shop from a vast array of eligible items across various categories, including apparel, home goods, electronics, and more. Walmart has assured that orders will be delivered through the same trusted network that serves millions of customers in the United States daily. Shipping and customs clearance will be managed by established international carriers to ensure reliable delivery.

To celebrate the launch, Walmart is offering a limited-time promotion for orders shipping to Mexico, including free shipping on eligible orders of $35 or more. The company has also indicated plans to expand its international shipping capabilities to additional markets in the future, marking a significant step in its global strategy.

Mexico has long been a key international market for Walmart. May 28, 2026: Walmart Partners with Teladoc to Enhance Virtual Care Services

Walmart has announced a strategic partnership with Teladoc Health, bringing the telehealth provider's virtual care services to its Better Care Services platform. As of 29th May 2026, this collaboration aims to enhance the healthcare experience for Walmart customers by providing access to a range of services including virtual urgent care, dermatology, and nutrition consultations.

The newly integrated services allow both insured and cash-pay customers to access Teladoc's offerings at a competitive price of $89 per visit. The virtual urgent care service addresses common health issues such as sinus infections and urinary tract infections, while dermatology consultations promise a diagnosis within 24 hours from board-certified specialists. Additionally, nutrition services will offer personalized consultations for various health concerns, including diabetes management and prenatal nutrition.

Kelly Bliss, President of U.S. Group Health at Teladoc Health, emphasized the convenience of accessing healthcare through Walmart, stating, "Walmart is where millions of Americans already go for everyday needs, and now, getting care from Teladoc Health can be part of that same experience." The collaboration follows an earlier introduction of Teladoc's BetterHelp mental health services on Walmart's platform, further expanding the range of healthcare options available to consumers.

Teladoc Health, which operates the largest nationwide network of virtual care providers, reported a revenue of $614 million for Q1 2026, surpassing projections of $611.36 million. However, the company's earnings per share came in at -$0.36, slightly below the anticipated -$0.3412. The partnership with Walmart aligns with Teladoc's strategy to diversify its service offerings and improve financial performance, as analysts have noted an upward trend in the company's stock outlook amid these developments.

Analyst firms have responded positively to the news, with Jefferies raising its price target for Teladoc Health to $6.00 and BofA Securities increasing its target to $9.00 while maintaining a Buy rating. Jun 16, 2026: Walmart's New Braunfels Distribution Center to Undergo $8M Automation Upgrade

Walmart is set to initiate a significant renovation of its distribution center in New Braunfels, Texas, with a budget of $8 million. The project is scheduled to commence on August 17, 2026, and is expected to be completed by September 17, 2027. This renovation phase will focus on selective demolition, the installation of new electrical systems, enhanced material-handling equipment, and upgrades to fire suppression and compressed air systems, as detailed in a filing with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation.

This ongoing renovation reflects Walmart's broader strategy to automate its distribution network and optimize operational costs. The retail giant has identified automation as a crucial element in managing its primary cost drivers: inventory and labor. Earlier this year, Walmart executives highlighted that capital spending on supply chain improvements is likely to peak in the coming years, with automation accounting for a significant share of this investment. Currently, Walmart is upgrading 23 of its 42 regional distribution centers with advanced automation technology, with plans to eventually modernize all facilities in its network.

Walmart has previously indicated that automation contributes to reduced shipping costs by improving operational efficiency. Presently, more than 60% of the retailer's U.S. locations receive goods from automated distribution centers. This strategic move towards automation is designed to enhance efficiency across Walmart's supply chain, allowing the company to respond more effectively to changing market demands.

While Walmart did not provide additional details about the New Braunfels project, the investment aligns with the company's goal of streamlining its distribution processes. As Walmart continues to modernize its operations, it is likely to maintain its competitive edge in an increasingly automated retail landscape. The commitment to upgrading the New Braunfels facility underscores Walmart's focus on leveraging technology to drive growth and operational excellence.

As Walmart embarks on this $8 million renovation, stakeholders and investors will be closely monitoring the outcomes of its automation initiatives. The New Braunfels distribution center's remodel may serve as a bellwether for Walmart's future investments in technology-driven efficiencies, reinforcing the company's position as a leader in the retail sector.

Jun 15, 2026: Walmart (NYSE: WMT) Sets Sights on E-Commerce Growth with Cross-Border Shipping

Walmart Inc. (NYSE: WMT) is accelerating its global e-commerce push with a string of moves designed to expand reach and speed up fulfillment for customers worldwide. On 11th June 2026, the retail giant opened Walmart.com to customers in Mexico, granting access to hundreds of thousands of eligible items spanning apparel, home goods, electronics, and more.

This international expansion marks a significant shift in how Walmart approaches its online marketplace, moving well beyond its traditional domestic pickup and delivery model. Duties, taxes, and fees are displayed at checkout for cross-border orders, giving Mexican customers full pricing transparency before completing their purchases. Walmart has also confirmed plans to extend international shipping to additional markets in the future, signaling that the Mexico launch is just the first step in a broader global strategy.

On the domestic front, Walmart announced on 28th May that 30-minute-or-less delivery is now available across 33 U.S. markets, covering more than 100,000 eligible items. Products available for rapid delivery include groceries, pharmacy items, household supplies, pet food, electronics, and prescriptions, making the service broadly useful for everyday shopping needs.

In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Walmart reported that global e-commerce grew 26%, with Walmart U.S. e-commerce and Walmart International e-commerce growing 26% and 27% respectively. Store-fulfilled delivery has more than doubled over the past two years, with more than 36% of U.S. orders in the quarter delivered in under three hours.

The combination of rapid domestic delivery and expanding international access positions Walmart as a formidable competitor in the global e-commerce landscape, challenging pure-play online retailers on multiple fronts. With international shipping infrastructure now taking shape and domestic fulfillment networks continuing to mature, Walmart appears well-positioned to sustain its e-commerce momentum through the remainder of fiscal 2027.

This is a milestone in the evolution of how people access Walmart.com's marketplace assortment around the world, and we're excited to bring it to Mexico first."

Customers in Mexico will now be able to shop from a vast array of eligible items across various categories, including apparel, home goods, electronics, and more. Walmart has assured that orders will be delivered through the same trusted network that serves millions of customers in the United States daily. Shipping and customs clearance will be managed by established international carriers to ensure reliable delivery.

To celebrate the launch, Walmart is offering a limited-time promotion for orders shipping to Mexico, including free shipping on eligible orders of $35 or more. The company has also indicated plans to expand its international shipping capabilities to additional markets in the future, marking a significant step in its global strategy.

Mexico has long been a key international market for Walmart. May 28, 2026: Walmart Partners with Teladoc to Enhance Virtual Care Services

Walmart has announced a strategic partnership with Teladoc Health, bringing the telehealth provider's virtual care services to its Better Care Services platform. As of 29th May 2026, this collaboration aims to enhance the healthcare experience for Walmart customers by providing access to a range of services including virtual urgent care, dermatology, and nutrition consultations.

The newly integrated services allow both insured and cash-pay customers to access Teladoc's offerings at a competitive price of $89 per visit. The virtual urgent care service addresses common health issues such as sinus infections and urinary tract infections, while dermatology consultations promise a diagnosis within 24 hours from board-certified specialists. Additionally, nutrition services will offer personalized consultations for various health concerns, including diabetes management and prenatal nutrition.

Kelly Bliss, President of U.S. Group Health at Teladoc Health, emphasized the convenience of accessing healthcare through Walmart, stating, "Walmart is where millions of Americans already go for everyday needs, and now, getting care from Teladoc Health can be part of that same experience." The collaboration follows an earlier introduction of Teladoc's BetterHelp mental health services on Walmart's platform, further expanding the range of healthcare options available to consumers.

Teladoc Health, which operates the largest nationwide network of virtual care providers, reported a revenue of $614 million for Q1 2026, surpassing projections of $611.36 million. However, the company's earnings per share came in at -$0.36, slightly below the anticipated -$0.3412. The partnership with Walmart aligns with Teladoc's strategy to diversify its service offerings and improve financial performance, as analysts have noted an upward trend in the company's stock outlook amid these developments.

Analyst firms have responded positively to the news, with Jefferies raising its price target for Teladoc Health to $6.00 and BofA Securities increasing its target to $9.00 while maintaining a Buy rating. These adjustments reflect confidence in Teladoc's ability to navigate the evolving healthcare landscape and capitalize on its partnership with Walmart to enhance service delivery and financial stability.

SECTION 4 CORPORATE PROFILE

4.1 Activities

Arca Continental SAB de CV, a prominent Mexican conglomerate, is primarily engaged in the production, bottling, and distribution of beverages as a key franchise partner for The Coca-Cola Company. The company operates across Mexico, the United States, and South America, offering a diverse portfolio that includes carbonated soft drinks, bottled water, juices, teas, and snacks. Its core activities encompass manufacturing, logistics, and sales through an extensive network of distribution channels, serving both retail and hospitality sectors. In recent years, the fastest-growing segments have been healthier beverage options, such as flavored waters and ready-to-drink teas, driven by shifting consumer preferences toward wellness and hydration products. Additionally, international expansion into markets like Ecuador and Peru has fueled growth, enhancing revenue streams and market share. Arca Continental's strategic investments in sustainability and digital technologies further support its operational efficiency and long-term competitiveness in the global beverage industry. It is Mexico's largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

Just days before León XIV's first visit to Peru as pontiff, it continues to be revealed which famous individuals may have some type of contact with Robert Francis Prevost, who has a close connection to the country. In addition to Lita Pezo and Tania Libertad, on Tuesday, November 3, the singer Susana Baca herself revealed that she will have the opportunity to perform for the highest representative of the Catholic Church.

Through her social media, Susana Baca expressed her excitement upon confirming that she will sing to the 'Peruvian Pope' during his visit to Peru, scheduled from November 11 to 16. "I am a fortunate woman. My path today is filled with light, a lot of light, peace, and joy," stated Baca, who has voiced her opposition to the creation of the College of Artists.

Susana Baca delighted to sing for Pope León XIV

Susana Baca, who took a stance during the presidential elections, expressed her happiness to be among the artists performing for Pope León XIV and promised to do so with all her heart. Thus, she informed the media that she will not give any interviews as she wants to focus on "that wonderful event."

  • Susana Baca: "Artists, free thinkers, we are threatened"
  • Susana Baca surprises by revealing who she will support this Sunday in the runoff: "I will not spoil my vote, this is not the time for that"

"I have been asked to sing to the Pope when he visits our Peru, a country that he knows in its essence more than many. A Peru that he carries within himself... to the roots. I would like my song that day to embody the essence and power to convey everything that the women and men of our land would like to say. I will go out to sing with my heart lifted to God," she shared on her social media.

Furthermore, Baca indicated that she will only speak on the matter after her experience with the Pope. "I ask for understanding from those who would like to know more. But these sacred acts are not meant to be displayed; rather, they are acts of reflection, sacred and spiritual. I do believe, however, that the cry of everyone to the Pope is that he prays for the Peru we so desperately need. The Peru that requires his reconciliation," she concluded.

While the United States voted on the formation of its new Congress, another decision with regional implications was being finalized at a hotel in Miraflores. The other countries that have already signed this agreement are Ecuador, the Dominican Republic, Colombia, and El Salvador.

In this case, the aim is for the Peruvian state to advance with a power generation technology that is not yet in operation in the country. They announced an initial funding of one million dollars to be allocated for technical assistance and training. This initial amount, according to sources consulted by this newspaper at the IPEN, is not explicitly detailed in the memorandum, meaning that it is still unclear how these resources will be distributed and that "this aspect has not yet been evaluated."

Under Secretary DiNanno presented it as a starting point. "As we do in everything, we start with a million and then we go up," he asserted. Regarding the timing of the announcement, La República asked him about the chosen moment, and he stated that "we have a small window, really turbocharged," explaining that as soon as the government changed, with Keiko Fujimori in power since July 28, it was necessary to devise a plan to show Peruvians that the United States is the "partner of choice."

"Safety First"

At the press conference, the Under Secretary emphasized the need for caution. "It has to be safety first," he affirmed. He added that a nuclear license in the United States requires a very high list of requirements, stating, "we cannot trade speed for safety."

In this regard, Washington is offering its Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to help Peru establish its own regulatory authority. "The NRC is, by far, the world leader in this," DiNanno stated. For this, it is crucial to start with small modular reactors, known in English as SMRs, and microreactors, compact plants that are made up of modular components.

U.S. Ambassador to Peru Bernie Navarro envisioned specific applications. "For mines located in desolate areas, perhaps a microsystem could help provide them with energy. Data centers, which require a lot of electricity for the grid, could perhaps use one of these microreactors for their operations," he commented.

The Program Behind the Agreement

Behind the memorandum is FIRST, a program from the State Department launched in 2021 under former President Joe Biden's administration, created to assist over 60 countries in developing small modular reactors using standards from the International Atomic Energy Agency.

Peru arrives at this memorandum with some groundwork already laid. The Peruvian Institute of Nuclear Energy, under the Ministry of Energy and Mines, operates the RP-10 research reactor in Carabayllo, north of Lima, which produces radioisotopes for medicine. Currently produced isotopes include technetium-99m for organ imaging studies and iodine-131 used to treat thyroid diseases and some cancer treatments .

Peru currently lacks a nuclear power generation plant, as the RP-10 is a research reactor. The Law 32560, enacted in March to promote nuclear generation and SMRs, led the Ministry of Energy and Mines to draft a roadmap toward 2040, a timeline that Washington hopes to expedite.

The IPEN, under the Ministry of Energy and Mines, stated in response to La República that the vision of this memorandum is for the country to have new options in the future to strengthen its energy security and meet continuous electricity needs in remote areas, such as some communities in the Amazon. This could contribute, they added, to guaranteeing essential services like hospitals, health centers, and schools. However, this differs from the potential uses mentioned by high-ranking U.S. officials, who referred to data centers, mines, and ports as potential applications.

In this context, the head of the Peruvian Ministry of Energy and Mines warned that the success of the initiative "depends not only on technical capabilities or an appropriate regulatory framework but also on the trust and informed participation of society."

On September 28 , the U.S. Embassy announced that Peru, already a participant in the program, would become a bilateral partner. El Salvador, the most advanced, signed its memorandum with Secretary of State Marco Rubio in February 2025 and plans to have its first reactor operational by 2030, according to Salvadoran press reports. Ecuador followed in April 2026, the Dominican Republic in June, and Colombia in September.

"We Are Here First," The Geopolitics of Nuclear Cooperation

Signings are occurring with increasingly shorter intervals, from San Salvador to Asunción and now Lima. Ambassador Navarro stated that "not all nuclear power suppliers are the same" and that "this is why we are here first," attributing this to American technology as compared to Russian and Chinese alternatives, while not downplaying the merits of European technology.

During the press conference, he mentioned that his government aims to ensure there is no dependence on the electricity grid of Lima, calling it important for the country. In the discussion, a colleague asked him if he imagined a scenario where Chinese companies could turn off the lights in the capital, which could threaten national security. The ambassador avoided confirming or dismissing such a scenario. "I'm not speculating. My job is not to speculate about that, but to ensure that I bring technologies that help Peru have a better daily life," he stated.

The context adds a concrete dimension to this dialogue. The two electric distribution companies serving Lima are currently owned by Chinese state enterprises. Luz del Sur is owned by China Three Gorges, and Pluz Energía, previously Enel Distribución and with a concession in northern Lima and Callao, belongs to China Southern Power Grid, whose acquisition for around $3.1 billion was finalized in June 2024 after conditional approval from Indecopi. During this transaction, the National Society of Industries warned about a total market concentration in Lima's distribution. Four years earlier, with the sale of Luz del Sur to Chinese capital, Osinergmin, which sets distribution rates, had assured that the operation "would not affect the electricity rates of its users" and would oversee energy purchases from related companies.

Nuclear Use, but Civil

The term refers to the use of nuclear energy for electricity production, manufacturing medicines, and conducting research, as opposed to the military branch, which seeks weapons or naval propulsion. The physics for both purposes are the same. The difference lies in the design and in the oversight of the IAEA, which verifies that uranium and plutonium do not end up in weapons. Peru operates a research reactor under that oversight and approved an additional protocol in 2001 that expands verification measures.

Two issues remain unresolved. Regarding military use, the official response is limited. The Under Secretary's own words place the process at a very early stage, as his goal is, he stated, "to identify a site," meaning that the one million dollars is intended to fund "feasibility studies." Among the potential applications of a microreactor, he mentioned "a data center, a port, a military base," although no concrete project for Peru has been announced so far.

On the other hand, the visit saw the addition of 20 million dollars from the State Department for aerial refueling of the F-16 Block 70 and 4.5 million for the Naval Base of Callao.

Beyond the symbolism of the act, the formal scope of the document is limited, as it is a non-binding civil nuclear cooperation agreement between states. Practically, it establishes a political intent and opens a pathway for technical assistance and training, without creating legal obligations for either party at this moment. Any transfer of technology or nuclear material would require a subsequent instrument, known as a 123 agreement, which would indeed be binding and does not currently appear on the announced agenda.

• Los ingresos por la producción de arenas bituminosas se disparan un 32 % hasta alcanzar los 9.32 mil millones de dólares canadienses en el trimestre
  • Tanto la producción en la fase de exploración y producción como el volumen de procesamiento de las refinerías disminuyeron en el tercer trimestre
  • Suncor aumentó la recompra mensual de acciones a 750 millones de dólares canadienses a partir de octubre

Se añaden detalles y contexto a lo largo del texto

3 nov (Reuters) - La productora integrada de petróleo y gas canadiense Suncor Energy SU.TO superó el martes las expectativas de los analistas en cuanto a beneficios del tercer trimestre, ya que el aumento de los precios del petróleo y la solidez de los márgenes de refino ayudaron a compensar la disminución de los volúmenes de producción y procesamiento.

La guerra de Irán (link), que ya entra en su noveno mes, ha perturbado el suministro energético mundial, lo que ha provocado un aumento de los precios del crudo. El precio medio del crudo de referencia Brent se situó en 89,27 dólares por barril durante el trimestre, un 31 % más que el año anterior.

Las empresas petroleras integradas, como Imperial Oil IMO.TO y Suncor, se han beneficiado de un mercado mundial de combustibles agitado por la guerra, ya que el aumento de los precios del petróleo ha reforzado los márgenes tanto en la producción como en el refinado.

La semana pasada, Imperial Oil IMO.TO también superó las previsiones de los analistas en cuanto a beneficios trimestrales, gracias a los sólidos márgenes de refino.

Durante el trimestre, Suncor registró una caída tanto en la producción en la fase inicial como en los volúmenes de procesamiento. Sin embargo, el aumento de los precios del petróleo contribuyó a que los ingresos procedentes de la producción de arenas bituminosas se incrementaran un 32 %, hasta alcanzar los 9.32 mil millones de dólares canadienses (6.66 mil millones de dólares).

Los ingresos procedentes de sus operaciones de refino se dispararon más del 65 %, hasta alcanzar unos 13 400 millones de dólares canadienses, impulsados por un aumento de más del doble en los márgenes de craqueo de referencia, lo que permitió a las refinerías obtener beneficios significativamente mayores por el procesamiento de cada barril de crudo.

La producción upstream de la empresa, con sede en Calgary (Alberta), cayó un 2 %, hasta los 852 500 barriles diarios, mientras que el volumen de procesamiento de las refinerías descendió ligeramente hasta los 487 700 bpd.

Suncor anunció un dividendo trimestral de 66 céntimos canadienses por acción, pagadero el 24 de diciembre, lo que supone un aumento del 10 % con respecto al trimestre anterior.

En octubre, Suncor acordó vender sus participaciones (link) en tres activos petroleros en alta mar de Canadá a Ithaca ITH.L por 1.200 millones de dólares canadienses y aumentó las recompras de acciones de 500 millones a 750 millones de dólares canadienses al mes a partir de octubre.

La empresa registró un beneficio operativo ajustado de 3,97 dólares canadienses por acción en el trimestre finalizado el 30 de septiembre, frente a la estimación media de los analistas de 3,28 dólares canadienses por acción, según datos recopilados por LSEG.

(1 dólar = 1,3998 dólares canadienses)

Sin embargo, el aumento de los precios del petróleo contribuyó a que los ingresos procedentes de la producción de arenas bituminosas se incrementaran un 32 %, hasta alcanzar los 9.32 mil millones de dólares canadienses (6.66 mil millones de dólares).

Los ingresos procedentes de sus operaciones de refino se dispararon más del 65 %, hasta alcanzar unos 13 400 millones de dólares canadienses, impulsados por un aumento de más del doble en los márgenes de craqueo de referencia, lo que permitió a las refinerías obtener beneficios significativamente mayores por el procesamiento de cada barril de crudo.

La producción upstream de la empresa, con sede en Calgary (Alberta), cayó un 2 %, hasta los 852 500 barriles diarios, mientras que el volumen de procesamiento de las refinerías descendió ligeramente hasta los 487 700 bpd.

Suncor anunció un dividendo trimestral de 66 céntimos canadienses por acción, pagadero el 24 de diciembre, lo que supone un aumento del 10 % con respecto al trimestre anterior.

En octubre, Suncor acordó vender sus participaciones (link) en tres activos petroleros en alta mar de Canadá a Ithaca ITH.L por 1.200 millones de dólares canadienses y aumentó las recompras de acciones de 500 millones a 750 millones de dólares canadienses al mes a partir de octubre.

La empresa registró un beneficio operativo ajustado de 3,97 dólares canadienses por acción en el trimestre finalizado el 30 de septiembre, frente a la estimación media de los analistas de 3,28 dólares canadienses por acción, según datos recopilados por LSEG.
